title.raw: 卷45 列傳第10 文四子 Volume 45 Biographies 10: Wen Sizi

sentences.zh: 房陵王勇，字睍地伐，高祖長子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Fangling Yang Yong, courtesy name Yandiba, was the eldest son of Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yong, Prince of Fangling, whose courtesy name was Yandiba, was the eldest son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 周世，以太祖軍功封博平侯。

translations.literal: During the Zhou dynasty, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Boping for the military achievements of the Imperial Founder.
translations.idiomatic: In the Northern Zhou period, he was made Marquis of Boping on account of his grandfather Yang Zhong's military service.

sentences.zh: 及高祖輔政，立為世子，拜大將軍、左司衛，封長寧郡公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became regent, Yong was established as heir apparent, appointed General-in-Chief and Left Commander of the Palace Guard, and enfeoffed as Duke of Changning Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen assumed the regency, Yong was named heir apparent, appointed General-in-Chief and Left Commander of the Palace Guard, and created Duke of Changning.

sentences.zh: 出為洛州總管、東京小塚宰，總統舊齊之地。

translations.literal: He was sent out to serve as Governor-General of Luozhou and Junior Steward of the Eastern Capital, overseeing the former territory of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Governor-General of Luozhou and Junior Steward of the Eastern Capital, with overall authority over the former Qi territories.

sentences.zh: 後征還京師，進位上柱國、大司馬，領內史禦正，諸禁衛皆屬焉。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned back to the capital, promoted to Grand Preceptor of State and Grand Marshal, put in charge of the Inner Scribe Directorate and Imperial Censorate, and all palace guards were placed under his authority.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled to the capital, promoted to Grand Preceptor of State and Grand Marshal, and given charge of the Inner Scribe Directorate and Imperial Censorate, with all palace guards under his command.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，立為皇太子，軍國政事及尚書奏死罪已下，皆令勇參決之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Yong was installed as crown prince. Military and state affairs, and all memorials to the Ministry of State Affairs concerning crimes below capital punishment, were all submitted to Yong for joint decision.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Yong was made crown prince. Matters of war and government, and all Ministry of State Affairs memorials on offenses short of capital crimes, were referred to Yong for his decision.

sentences.zh: 上以山東民多流冗，遣使按檢，又欲徙民北實邊塞。

translations.literal: The emperor, noting that many people in the Shandong region were vagrant and unsettled, dispatched emissaries to investigate, and also intended to relocate commoners northward to populate the border fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, seeing that many people in the eastern provinces were displaced and idle, sent officials to investigate and also planned to resettle population northward to strengthen the frontier.

sentences.zh: 勇上書諫曰：「竊以導俗當漸，非可頓革，戀土懷舊，民之本情，波迸流離，蓋不獲已。

translations.literal: Yong submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying: 'I venture to think that guiding custom should be gradual and cannot be abruptly changed. Attachment to one's native soil and longing for home are the people's fundamental feelings. Their scattering and wandering are largely matters beyond their control.
translations.idiomatic: Yong submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "I believe that changing custom must be gradual—it cannot be done all at once. Love of home and attachment to native soil are the people's deepest instincts; their flight and dispersion are largely forced upon them.

sentences.zh: 有齊之末，主暗時昏，周平東夏，繼以威虐，民不堪命，致有逃亡，非厭家鄉，願為羈旅。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi, the ruler was benighted and the times were dark. Zhou pacified the eastern lands and followed with tyranny and cruelty. The people could not endure their lot, which led to flight—it was not that they despised their homelands and wished to become wanderers.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qi the rulers were corrupt and the times chaotic; when Zhou conquered the east, harsh rule followed, and the people could not bear it and fled—not because they hated their homes and wished to live as exiles.

sentences.zh: 加以去年三方逆亂，賴陛下仁聖，區宇肅清，鋒刃雖屏，瘡痍未複。

translations.literal: Moreover, last year rebellion arose on three fronts. Thanks to Your Majesty's benevolence and sagacity, the realm was pacified. Though the swords have been sheathed, the wounds have not yet healed.
translations.idiomatic: Then last year rebellions broke out on three fronts; thanks to Your Majesty's benevolence and wisdom the realm was pacified, but though the fighting has ceased, the wounds have not yet healed.

sentences.zh: 若假以數歲，沐浴皇風，逃竄之徒，自然歸本。

translations.literal: If they are given several years to bathe in the imperial influence, those who have fled will naturally return to their roots.
translations.idiomatic: If they are given a few years to enjoy the emperor's benevolent rule, those who fled will naturally return home.

sentences.zh: 雖北夷猖獗，嘗犯邊烽，今城鎮峻峙，所在嚴固，何待遷配，以致勞擾。

translations.literal: Although the northern barbarians are rampant and have sometimes violated the border beacons, the towns and fortresses now stand tall and are everywhere strong and secure. Why must people be relocated, causing labor and disturbance?
translations.idiomatic: Though the northern tribes are unruly and have sometimes raided the frontier, the garrison towns are now strong and secure everywhere—why resort to forced resettlement and cause such hardship?

sentences.zh: 臣以庸虛，謬當儲貳，寸誠管見，輒以塵聞。」

translations.literal: Your subject, being mediocre and empty, is wrongly placed as heir apparent. This inch of sincerity and narrow view I venture to offer before Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy in my station as heir apparent, yet I offer this humble opinion in all sincerity.

sentences.zh: 上覽而嘉之，遂寢其事。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and praised it, and thereupon shelved the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with approval and dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 是後時政不便，多所損益，上每納之。

translations.literal: After this, whenever current policy was inconvenient, Yong proposed many modifications and additions, and the emperor always accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever government policy seemed flawed, Yong proposed changes, and the emperor usually accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 上嘗從容謂群臣曰：「前世皇王，溺於嬖幸，廢立之所由生。

translations.literal: The emperor once said at ease to his ministers: 'Emperors and kings of previous ages, drowning in favorites, were the source from which deposition and installation arose.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once remarked casually to his ministers: "Emperors of past ages who indulged in favorites were the very cause of depositions and succession crises.

sentences.zh: 朕傍無姬侍，五子同母，可謂真兄弟也。

translations.literal: I have no concubines at my side; my five sons share the same mother—they may be called true brothers.
translations.idiomatic: I have no concubines at court, and my five sons are all born of the same mother—they are true brothers indeed.

sentences.zh: 豈若前代多諸內寵，孽子忿諍，為亡國之道邪！」

translations.literal: How could this be like previous ages with many inner favorites, illegitimate sons in angry contention—the path to losing a state!"
translations.idiomatic: How unlike earlier dynasties, with their many favored consorts and rival sons of different mothers—the very road to ruin!"

sentences.zh: 勇頗好學，解屬詞賦，性寬仁和厚，率意任情，無矯飾之行。

translations.literal: Yong was quite fond of learning, skilled at composing prose and poetry, by nature generous, benevolent, and sincere, following his inclinations and acting on his feelings, with no pretense in his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was studious and skilled at literary composition; he was generous, kind, and sincere by nature, acting naturally without affectation.

sentences.zh: 引明克讓、姚察、陸開明等為之賓友。

translations.literal: He invited Ming Kerang, Yao Cha, Lu Kaiming, and others to serve as his guests and friends.
translations.idiomatic: He took Ming Kerang, Yao Cha, Lu Kaiming, and others as literary companions.

sentences.zh: 勇嘗文飾蜀鎧，上見而不悅，恐致奢侈之漸，因而誡之曰：「我聞天道無親，唯德是與，曆觀前代帝王，未有奢華而得長久者。

translations.literal: Yong once ornamented a suit of Shu armor with decorative writing. The emperor saw it and was displeased, fearing it might lead to gradual extravagance, and therefore admonished him, saying: 'I have heard that Heaven's Way is impartial and grants favor only to the virtuous. Looking through the emperors of previous ages, none who were extravagant achieved lasting rule.
translations.idiomatic: Yong once had a suit of Shu armor decorated with ornamental inscriptions. The emperor saw it and was displeased, fearing the first step toward extravagance, and admonished him: "Heaven favors virtue, not luxury—I have never seen an extravagant emperor whose dynasty endured.

sentences.zh: 汝當儲後，若不上稱天心，下合人意，何以承宗廟之重，居兆民之上？

translations.literal: You are to be the heir. If you do not accord with Heaven's heart above and the people's wishes below, how can you bear the weight of the ancestral temple and sit above the myriad people?
translations.idiomatic: You are the heir apparent—if you do not meet Heaven's expectations and the people's wishes, how can you bear the ancestral temple and rule over the masses?

sentences.zh: 吾昔日衣服，各留一物，時複看之，以自警戒。

translations.literal: I have kept one item from each of my old garments and sometimes look at them again to warn myself.
translations.idiomatic: I have kept one piece from each of my old garments and look at them from time to time to remind myself.

sentences.zh: 今以刀子賜汝，宜識我心。」

translations.literal: Now I bestow this knife upon you—you should understand my heart."
translations.idiomatic: I give you this knife now—remember what I mean by it."

sentences.zh: 其後經冬至，百官朝勇，勇張樂受賀。

translations.literal: Afterward, when the winter solstice arrived, the hundred officials paid court to Yong. Yong set out music and received congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the winter solstice, officials came to congratulate Yong at the Eastern Palace, where he held a celebration with music.

sentences.zh: 高祖知之，問朝臣曰：「近聞至節，內外百官相率朝東宮，是何禮也？」

translations.literal: Gaozu learned of this and asked the court ministers: 'I have recently heard that at the solstice, officials inside and outside the court all went in succession to pay court at the Eastern Palace—what sort of ritual is this?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen learned of this and asked his ministers: "I hear that at the solstice all the officials went to the Eastern Palace to pay their respects—what kind of ceremony is that?

sentences.zh: 太常少卿辛亶對曰：「于東宮是賀，不得言朝。」

translations.literal: Junior Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Xin Dan replied: 'At the Eastern Palace it was congratulations—it cannot be called paying court.'
translations.idiomatic: Junior Director of Sacrifices Xin Dan replied: "At the Eastern Palace it was a congratulatory visit, not a formal audience."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「改節稱賀，正可三數十人，逐情各去。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: 'Changing the solstice into congratulations—only thirty or so people would be appropriate, each going as they wish.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said: "If the solstice is to be marked with congratulations, a few dozen people at most should go as they please.

sentences.zh: 何因有司徵召，一時普集，太子法服設樂以待之？

translations.literal: Why did the responsible officials summon everyone, gathering them all at once, with the crown prince in formal robes setting out music to await them?
translations.idiomatic: Why did officials summon everyone at once, with the crown prince in full regalia and music prepared to receive them?

sentences.zh: 東宮如此，殊乖禮制。」

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace acting thus greatly deviates from ritual propriety.'
translations.idiomatic: Conduct like this at the Eastern Palace is a serious breach of protocol."

sentences.zh: 於是下詔曰：「禮有等差，君臣不雜，爰自近代，聖教漸虧，俯仰逐情，因循成俗。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued, saying: 'Ritual has gradations of rank; ruler and subject must not be mixed. From recent times, sagely instruction has gradually declined; bowing and rising follow personal inclination, and custom has formed through inertia.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued: "Ritual distinguishes rank and keeps ruler and subject separate; in recent times these distinctions have eroded, and custom has formed through careless habit.

sentences.zh: 皇太子雖居上嗣，義兼臣子，而諸方嶽牧，正冬朝賀，任土作貢，別上東宮，事非典則，宜悉停斷。」

translations.literal: Although the crown prince occupies the position of supreme heir and in principle is also a subject, for regional governors at the winter solstice to pay congratulations, present local products as tribute, and separately submit them to the Eastern Palace is not according to canonical norms—all such practices should be entirely stopped.'
translations.idiomatic: Though the crown prince is the heir, he is still a subject; for regional governors to bring winter solstice greetings and tribute separately to the Eastern Palace is improper—all such visits are hereby forbidden."

sentences.zh: 自此恩寵始衰，漸生疑阻。

translations.literal: From this point favor and grace began to decline, and suspicion and obstruction gradually arose.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the emperor's favor waned, and mutual suspicion grew.

sentences.zh: 時高祖令選宗衛侍官，以入上臺宿衛。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu ordered the selection of palace guard attendants from the imperial clan to enter the upper platform for night watch.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Wen ordered the selection of palace guard attendants from the imperial clan for duty at the upper palace.

sentences.zh: 高熲奏稱，若盡取強者，恐東宮宿衛太劣。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong memorialized, saying that if all the strongest were taken, he feared the Eastern Palace night watch would be too weak.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong reported that if all the strongest guards were taken, the Eastern Palace guard would be left too weak.

sentences.zh: 高祖作色曰：「我有時行動，宿衛須得雄毅。

translations.literal: Gaozu changed color and said: 'When I sometimes go out, the night watch must be bold and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's expression darkened: "When I travel, my guard must be strong and resolute.

sentences.zh: 太子毓德東宮，左右何須強武？

translations.literal: The crown prince cultivates virtue in the Eastern Palace—why do those at his side need to be strong warriors?
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince cultivates virtue in the Eastern Palace—why does he need fierce warriors at his side?

sentences.zh: 此極敝法，甚非我意。

translations.literal: This is an extremely corrupt practice and very much not my intention.
translations.idiomatic: This is a thoroughly bad practice and not at all what I want.

sentences.zh: 如我商量，恆於交番之日，分向東宮上下，團伍不別，豈非好事？

translations.literal: As I have considered it, on the days of rotation, dividing them between the upper and lower parts of the Eastern Palace without distinguishing units—would that not be a good arrangement?
translations.idiomatic: As I see it, on rotation days guards should be divided between the upper palace and the Eastern Palace without separate units—is that not better?

sentences.zh: 我熟見前代，公不須仍踵舊風。」

translations.literal: I am thoroughly familiar with previous ages—you, sir, need not still follow the old ways.
translations.idiomatic: I know the mistakes of past dynasties well—you need not follow their old ways.

sentences.zh: 蓋疑高熲男尚勇女，形於此言，以防之也。

translations.literal: This was probably because he suspected that Gao Jiong's son was married to Yong's daughter, and it showed in these words as a precaution against him.
translations.idiomatic: This was likely because he suspected Gao Jiong's son was married to Yong's daughter—the remark was meant as a warning.

sentences.zh: 勇多內寵，昭訓雲氏，尤稱嬖幸，禮匹於嫡。

translations.literal: Yong had many inner favorites; Lady Yun of Zhaoxun was especially called a cherished favorite, treated with ritual equal to the principal wife.
translations.idiomatic: Yong kept many concubines; Lady Yun of Zhaoxun was his especial favorite, treated with the honors due a principal wife.

sentences.zh: 勇妃元氏無寵，嘗遇心疾，二日而薨。

translations.literal: Yong's consort, Lady Yuan, was without favor. She once suffered a heart ailment and died within two days.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's principal consort, Lady Yuan, was unloved; she once fell ill with a heart condition and died within two days.

sentences.zh: 獻皇后意有他故，甚責望勇。

translations.literal: Empress Xian suspected there was another cause and greatly blamed and reproached Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dugu suspected foul play and severely reproached Yong.

sentences.zh: 自是雲昭訓專擅內政，後彌不平，頗遣人伺察，求勇罪過。

translations.literal: From this point Lady Yun Zhaoxun monopolized inner household affairs. The empress grew increasingly resentful and frequently sent people to spy and seek Yong's faults.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Lady Yun dominated the inner household; the empress grew ever more hostile and sent agents to watch Yong and find fault with him.

sentences.zh: 晉王知之，彌自矯飾，姬妾但備員數，唯共蕭妃居處。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin learned of this and all the more practiced self-restraint and ornamentation. His concubines were kept only to fill the roster; he lived only with Consort Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin, learning of this, became all the more careful in his conduct: he kept concubines only for show and lived exclusively with Consort Xiao.

sentences.zh: 皇后由是薄勇，愈稱晉王德行。

translations.literal: The empress therefore looked down on Yong and increasingly praised the Prince of Jin's virtue and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The empress accordingly lost regard for Yong and praised the Prince of Jin's character ever more highly.

sentences.zh: 其後晉王來朝，車馬侍從，皆為儉素，敬接朝臣，禮極卑屈，聲名籍甚，冠于諸王。

translations.literal: Afterward when the Prince of Jin came to court, his carriages, horses, and attendants were all plain and simple. He respectfully received court ministers with the utmost humility, and his reputation was greatly renowned, surpassing all the princes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin later came to court, his retinue was plain and modest; he treated ministers with extreme deference, and his reputation surpassed all the other princes.

sentences.zh: 臨還揚州，入內辭皇后，因進言曰：「臣鎮守有限，方違顏色，臣子之戀，實結於心。

translations.literal: On the eve of returning to Yangzhou, he entered the inner palace to bid farewell to the empress and thereupon offered words, saying: 'Your subject's garrison duty is limited; I am just now parting from Your Majesty's presence. A subject's attachment is truly bound in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Before returning to Yangzhou he went to bid the empress farewell and said: "My post keeps me far away, and I must leave Your Majesty's presence; a son's longing is deeply rooted in my heart.

sentences.zh: 一辭階闥，無由侍奉，拜見之期，杳然未日。」

translations.literal: Once I leave these steps and doors, I have no means to serve you. The day when I may bow and see you again is distant and without date.
translations.idiomatic: Once I leave these halls I cannot attend you, and the day I may see you again seems impossibly far.

sentences.zh: 因哽咽流涕，伏不能興。

translations.literal: Thereupon he choked with sobs and wept, prostrating himself and unable to rise.
translations.idiomatic: He broke into sobs, wept, and prostrated himself, unable to rise.

sentences.zh: 皇后亦曰：「汝在方鎮，我又年老，今者之別，有切常離。」

translations.literal: The empress also said: 'You are at a regional post and I am old. This parting today cuts deeper than ordinary separation.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "You are posted far away and I am old—this parting cuts deeper than the usual farewell.

sentences.zh: 又泫然泣下，相對歔欷。

translations.literal: She again shed tears and wept; facing each other they sighed with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Tears streamed down her face as they wept together.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「臣性識愚下，常守平生昆弟之意，不知何罪，失愛東宮，恆蓄盛怒，欲加屠陷。

translations.literal: The prince said: 'Your subject's nature and understanding are foolish and low. I have always kept to the brotherly feelings of our lifelong bond. I do not know what crime I have committed to lose the Eastern Palace's favor. He constantly harbors great anger and wishes to destroy me.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said: "I am dull by nature and have always kept brotherly affection, yet somehow I have lost the crown prince's favor; he constantly nurses anger and seeks to destroy me.

sentences.zh: 每恐讒譖生於投杼，鴆毒遇於杯勺，是用勤憂積念，懼履危亡。」

translations.literal: I constantly fear that slander will arise like the tale of the pestle, or that poison will meet me in cup and spoon. Therefore I am diligent in worry and accumulate anxious thoughts, fearing I will tread the path to ruin and death.
translations.idiomatic: I live in fear of slander and poison—I worry constantly that I am walking toward ruin.

sentences.zh: 皇后忿然曰：「睍地伐漸不可耐，我為伊索得元家女，望隆基業，竟不聞作夫妻，專寵阿雲，使有如許豚犬。

translations.literal: The empress said angrily: 'Yandiba is gradually becoming unbearable. I obtained a daughter of the Yuan family for him, hoping for the flourishing of the imperial enterprise, yet I never hear of them acting as husband and wife. He favors A-Yun exclusively and has produced such pig-and-dog offspring.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said angrily: "Yandiba is becoming intolerable. I found him a Yuan family bride, hoping for imperial heirs, yet they never act as husband and wife—he dotes on that Yun woman and has sired such worthless sons.

sentences.zh: 前新婦本無病痛，忽爾暴亡，遣人投藥，致此夭逝。

translations.literal: The former new bride originally had no illness or pain, yet suddenly she died violently. Someone was sent to administer poison, causing this untimely death.
translations.idiomatic: The new bride was perfectly healthy, then suddenly died—someone poisoned her and caused her early death.

sentences.zh: 事已如是，我亦不能窮治，何因複於汝處發如此意？

translations.literal: Matters being already thus, I also could not thoroughly investigate. Why then did such thoughts arise again on your account?
translations.idiomatic: I could not pursue the matter further—but why would you think he would do the same to you?

sentences.zh: 我在尚爾，我死後，當魚肉汝乎？

translations.literal: While I am still alive it is already like this—after I die, will he not treat you like fish on the chopping block?
translations.idiomatic: If this is how things are while I live, what will he do to you after I am gone?

sentences.zh: 每思東宮竟無正嫡，至尊千秋萬歲之後，遣汝等兄弟向阿雲兒前再拜問訊，此是幾許大苦痛邪！」

translations.literal: Whenever I think that the Eastern Palace ultimately has no legitimate principal heir—after the Supreme One's myriad autumns and ten thousand years, sending you brothers to bow twice before A-Yun's sons to pay respects—how great a pain is this!'
translations.idiomatic: When I think that after the emperor's death you brothers would have to bow before Yun's sons—what agony that would be!"

sentences.zh: 晉王又拜，嗚咽不能止，皇后亦悲不自勝。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin bowed again, sobbing without cease, and the empress also grieved beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin bowed again, sobbing uncontrollably, and the empress was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 此別之後，知皇后意移，始構奪宗之計。

translations.literal: After this parting, knowing the empress's mind had shifted, he began to devise a plan to seize the succession.
translations.idiomatic: After this farewell, seeing that the empress's favor had turned, he began plotting to seize the succession.

sentences.zh: 因引張衡定策，遣褒公宇文述深交楊約，令喻旨于越國公素，具言皇后此語。

translations.literal: He therefore enlisted Zhang Heng to settle the strategy, sent Duke of Bao Yuwen Shu to cultivate deep ties with Yang Yue, and had him convey the intent to Duke of Yueguo Su, fully reporting the empress's words.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted Zhang Heng to plan the strategy and sent Duke Yuwen Shu to cultivate Yang Yue, instructing him to convey the empress's words to Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 素瞿然曰：「但不知皇后如何？

translations.literal: Su started in alarm and said: 'I only do not know what the empress thinks?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su started and said: "But I do not know the empress's mind—

sentences.zh: 必如所言，吾又何為者！」

translations.literal: If it must be as you say, what further need is there for me!
translations.idiomatic: if it is truly as you say, what more need I do!

sentences.zh: 後數日，素入侍宴，微稱晉王孝悌恭儉，有類至尊，用此揣皇后意。

translations.literal: Several days later, Su entered to attend a banquet and subtly praised the Prince of Jin's filial piety, brotherly affection, respect, and frugality, saying he resembled the Supreme One, using this to gauge the empress's mind.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Yang Su attended a banquet and subtly praised the Prince of Jin's filial piety, humility, and frugality, saying he resembled the emperor, to test the empress's reaction.

sentences.zh: 皇后泣曰：「公言是也。

translations.literal: The empress wept and said: 'What you say is correct.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wept: "You are right.

sentences.zh: 我兒大孝順，每聞至尊及我遣內使到，必迎於境首。

translations.literal: My son is greatly filial. Whenever he hears that the Supreme One or I have sent inner emissaries, he always goes to meet them at the border of his territory.
translations.idiomatic: My son is deeply filial—whenever he hears the emperor or I have sent palace envoys, he meets them at the border of his province.

sentences.zh: 言及違離，未嘗不泣。

translations.literal: When speaking of separation, he has never failed to weep.
translations.idiomatic: He weeps whenever separation is mentioned.

sentences.zh: 又其新婦亦大可憐，我使婢去，常與之同寢共食。

translations.literal: Moreover his new bride is also greatly pitiable. When I send maidservants, they always sleep and eat together with her.
translations.idiomatic: His bride is also most endearing—when I send maidservants, they sleep and dine with her.

sentences.zh: 豈若睍地伐共阿雲相對而坐，終日酣宴，昵近小人，疑阻骨肉。

translations.literal: How could this compare with Yandiba sitting face to face with A-Yun, feasting all day, drawing close to petty men, and creating suspicion and obstruction between flesh and bone?
translations.idiomatic: How unlike Yandiba, who sits feasting all day with that Yun woman, consorts with low characters, and sows discord among brothers.

sentences.zh: 我所以益憐阿摐者，常恐暗地殺之。」

translations.literal: The reason I pity A-Chou all the more is that I constantly fear he will be secretly killed.
translations.idiomatic: I favor Guang all the more because I constantly fear Yong will have him killed in secret.

sentences.zh: 素既知意，因盛言太子不才。

translations.literal: Su, now knowing her intent, thereupon spoke at length of the crown prince's lack of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su, now understanding her mind, spoke at length of the crown prince's unfitness.

sentences.zh: 皇后遂遺素金，始有廢立之意。

translations.literal: The empress thereupon sent gold to Su, and the intention to depose and install began.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then sent gold to Yang Su, and the plan to depose Yong and install Guang began.

sentences.zh: 勇頗知其謀，憂懼，計無所出。

translations.literal: Yong was quite aware of their plot, anxious and fearful, with no plan to escape it.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had some inkling of the plot and was anxious and afraid, but could think of no remedy.

sentences.zh: 聞新豐人王輔賢能占候，召而問之。

translations.literal: He heard that Wang Fuxian of Xinfeng could perform divination and prognostication, and summoned him to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Wang Fuxian of Xinfeng could read omens, he summoned him for counsel.

sentences.zh: 輔賢曰：「白虹貫東宮門，太白襲月，皇太子廢退之象也。」

translations.literal: Fuxian said: 'A white rainbow pierces the Eastern Palace gate; the Great White star assaults the moon—these are signs of the crown prince's deposition and removal.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxian said: "A white rainbow spans the Eastern Palace gate, and Venus eclipses the moon—these are omens of the crown prince's deposition.

sentences.zh: 以銅鐵五兵造諸厭勝。

translations.literal: He had various apotropaic objects made from copper, iron, and the five weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had apotropaic charms fashioned from copper, iron, and the five weapons.

sentences.zh: 又于後園之內作庶人村，屋宇卑陋，太子時于中寢息，布衣草褥，冀以當之。

translations.literal: He also built a Commoners' Village in the rear garden, with humble and shabby dwellings. The crown prince sometimes slept and rested there on cloth garments and straw bedding, hoping thereby to substitute for his fate.
translations.idiomatic: He also built a "commoners' village" in the rear garden with humble dwellings, where he sometimes slept on straw bedding in plain clothes, hoping to avert his fate.

sentences.zh: 高祖知其不安，在仁壽宮，使楊素觀勇。

translations.literal: Gaozu knew he was unsettled. While at Renshou Palace, he sent Yang Su to observe Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, knowing Yong was uneasy, sent Yang Su from Renshou Palace to observe him.

sentences.zh: 素至東宮，偃息未入，勇束帶待之，故久不進，以激怒勇。

translations.literal: Su arrived at the Eastern Palace and rested without entering. Yong girded himself and waited, so Su deliberately did not enter for a long time in order to provoke Yong's anger.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su arrived at the Eastern Palace and lingered outside without entering; Yong dressed formally and waited, and Su deliberately delayed to provoke him.

sentences.zh: 勇銜之，形於言色。

translations.literal: Yong harbored resentment, and it showed in his words and expression.
translations.idiomatic: Yong nursed the insult, and it showed in his words and face.

sentences.zh: 素還，言勇怨望，恐有他變，願深防察。

translations.literal: Su returned and reported that Yong was resentful and discontent, feared there might be other changes, and wished for deep precaution and investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su reported back that Yong was resentful and discontent, feared further trouble, and urged close surveillance.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞素譖毀，甚疑之。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard Su's slander and destruction and became greatly suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, hearing Yang Su's accusations, grew deeply suspicious of Yong.

sentences.zh: 皇后又遣人伺覘東宮，纖介事皆聞奏，因加媒蘖，構成其罪。

translations.literal: The empress also sent people to spy on the Eastern Palace; the slightest matters were all reported, and slander was added to fabricate his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The empress also sent spies to the Eastern Palace; the smallest matters were reported, and slander was piled on to build a case against him.

sentences.zh: 高祖惑于邪議，遂疏忌勇。

translations.literal: Gaozu, deluded by evil counsel, thereupon grew distant and suspicious of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, swayed by malicious counsel, grew distant and wary of Yong.

sentences.zh: 乃于玄武門達至德門量置候人，以伺動靜，皆隨事奏聞。

translations.literal: He then placed watchers from Xuanwu Gate to Zhide Gate to observe movements, all reporting matters as they arose.
translations.idiomatic: He posted watchers from Xuanwu Gate to Zhide Gate to monitor Yong's movements and report everything.

sentences.zh: 又東宮宿衛之人，侍官已上，名藉悉令屬諸衛府，有健兒者，鹹屏去之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Eastern Palace night watch personnel, attendants and above—all their registers were ordered transferred to the various guard offices, and those who were strong warriors were all removed.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace guard roster was transferred to the regular guard offices, and all strong warriors were removed.

sentences.zh: 晉王又令段達私於東宮幸臣姬威，遺以財貨，令取太子消息，密告楊素。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin also had Duan Da secretly approach Yong's favored minister Ji Wei, bestowing goods upon him and ordering him to gather news of the crown prince and secretly report to Yang Su.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin also had Duan Da secretly approach Yong's favorite Ji Wei, bribing him to gather intelligence on the crown prince and report secretly to Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 於是內外喧謗，過失日聞。

translations.literal: Thereupon slander arose inside and outside, and faults were heard of daily.
translations.idiomatic: Slander spread inside and outside the palace, and reports of Yong's faults arrived daily.

sentences.zh: 段達脅姬威曰：「東宮罪過，主上皆知之矣，已奉密詔，定當廢立。

translations.literal: Duan Da threatened Ji Wei, saying: 'The Eastern Palace's crimes—the sovereign already knows them all. A secret edict has already been received; deposition and installation are certainly decided.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da threatened Ji Wei: "The emperor already knows all the crown prince's offenses; a secret edict has been issued—the succession will be changed.

sentences.zh: 君能靠之，則大富貴。」

translations.literal: If you, sir, can rely on this, then great wealth and honor will follow.
translations.idiomatic: If you cooperate, great wealth and honor await you.

sentences.zh: 威遂許諾。

translations.literal: Wei thereupon promised.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wei agreed.

sentences.zh: 九月壬子，車駕至自仁壽宮，翌日，禦大興殿，謂侍臣曰：「我新還京師，應開懷歡樂，不知何意，翻邑然愁苦？」

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the ninth month, the imperial carriage arrived from Renshou Palace. The next day, presiding at Daxing Hall, he said to the attending ministers: 'I have newly returned to the capital and ought to open my heart in joy. I do not know why, instead, I am deeply melancholy and distressed.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the ninth month the emperor returned from Renshou Palace; the next day, at Daxing Hall, he said to his ministers: "I have just returned to the capital and should be happy—why do I feel so deeply troubled?

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書牛弘對曰：「由臣等不稱職，故至尊憂勞。」

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Niu Hong replied: 'It is because we your subjects are not competent in our offices, therefore the Supreme One is worried and toiling.'
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Niu Hong replied: "It is because we ministers are unworthy that Your Majesty is troubled."

sentences.zh: 高祖既數聞讒譖，疑朝臣皆具委，故有斯問，冀聞太子之愆。

translations.literal: Gaozu had repeatedly heard slander and suspected that all the court ministers were fully informed, therefore he had this question, hoping to hear of the crown prince's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, having heard much slander, suspected the ministers all knew something and asked this question hoping to hear of the crown prince's faults.

sentences.zh: 弘為此對，大乖本旨。

translations.literal: Hong's reply greatly missed the original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong's answer completely missed the point.

sentences.zh: 高祖因作色謂東宮官屬曰：「仁壽宮去此不遠，而令我每還京師，嚴備仗衛，如入敵國。

translations.literal: Gaozu thereupon changed color and said to the Eastern Palace officials: 'Renshou Palace is not far from here, yet every time I return to the capital I must strictly prepare arms and guards, as if entering a hostile state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's expression darkened as he addressed the Eastern Palace officials: "Renshou Palace is not far away, yet every time I return to the capital I must travel under heavy guard, as if entering enemy territory.

sentences.zh: 我為患利，不脫衣臥。

translations.literal: I suffer from dysentery and do not remove my clothes to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: I suffer from dysentery and sleep without undressing.

sentences.zh: 昨夜欲得近廁，故在後房，恐有警急，還移就前殿。

translations.literal: Last night I wished to be near the privy, so I was in the rear chamber; fearing an emergency, I moved back to the front hall.
translations.idiomatic: Last night I needed to be near the privy and stayed in the rear chamber; fearing trouble, I moved to the front hall.

sentences.zh: 豈非爾輩欲壞我國家邪？」

translations.literal: Is it not that you people wish to ruin my state?
translations.idiomatic: Are you not trying to ruin the state?

sentences.zh: 於是執唐令則等數人，付所司訊鞫。

translations.literal: Thereupon he arrested Tang Lingze and several others and handed them over to the responsible offices for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: He then arrested Tang Lingze and several others and turned them over for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 令楊素陳東宮事狀，以告近臣。

translations.literal: He ordered Yang Su to set forth the circumstances of the Eastern Palace and report them to the close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yang Su to report the Eastern Palace affair to the inner circle of ministers.

sentences.zh: 素顯言之曰：「臣奉敕向京，令皇太子檢校劉居士餘黨。

translations.literal: Su spoke openly, saying: 'Your subject received the edict to go to the capital and ordered the crown prince to investigate the remaining followers of Liu Jushi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su spoke openly: "I received orders to go to the capital and instructed the crown prince to investigate the remaining followers of Liu Jushi.

sentences.zh: 太子奉詔，乃作色奮厲，骨肉飛騰，語臣雲：'居士党盡伏法，遣我何處窮討？

translations.literal: The crown prince received the edict and thereupon changed color and flared up fiercely, his flesh and bones trembling, saying to your subject: 'Liu Jushi's faction has all been executed by law—where am I to pursue further investigation?'
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince received the order but flushed with anger and said to me: 'Liu Jushi's followers have all been executed—where am I supposed to hunt further?'

sentences.zh: 爾作右僕射，委寄不輕，自檢校之，何關我事？

translations.literal: You serve as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs—the trust placed in you is not light. Investigate it yourself—what business is it of mine?
translations.idiomatic: You are Right Vice Director—the trust placed in you is great; investigate it yourself—what business is it of mine?

sentences.zh: '又雲：'若大事不遂，我先被誅。

translations.literal: He also said: 'If the great affair does not succeed, I will be the first to be executed.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'If great matters fail, I will be the first executed.'

sentences.zh: 今作天子，竟乃令我不如諸弟。

translations.literal: Now that I am to become Son of Heaven, he actually makes me inferior to my younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I am to become emperor, he actually makes me inferior to my younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 一事以上，不得自由。

translations.literal: In not a single matter am I allowed freedom.
translations.idiomatic: I am not free in a single matter.

sentences.zh: '因長歎回視雲：'我大覺身妨。

translations.literal: He then sighed deeply, turned, and looked back, saying: 'I greatly feel myself obstructed.'
translations.idiomatic: He sighed deeply, turned, and said: 'I feel greatly obstructed.'

sentences.zh: '」高祖曰：「此兒不堪承嗣久矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: 'This son has long been unfit to inherit the succession.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said: "This son has long been unfit to inherit."

sentences.zh: 皇后恆勸我廢之，我以布素時生，複是長子，望其漸改，隱忍至今。

translations.literal: The empress constantly urged me to depose him. Because he was born when we were still in plain cloth and he is moreover the eldest son, I hoped he would gradually reform and have endured in silence until now.
translations.idiomatic: The empress has constantly urged me to depose him; he was born when we were still commoners and he is the eldest son, so I hoped he would reform and have endured until now.

sentences.zh: 勇昔從南兗州來，語衛王雲：「阿娘不與我一好婦女，亦是可恨。」

translations.literal: Yong once came from Southern Yanzhou and said to the Prince of Wei: 'Mother did not give me a good woman—that is also hateful.'
translations.idiomatic: Yong once came from Southern Yanzhou and told the Prince of Wei: "Mother never gave me a good woman—that is also hateful."

sentences.zh: 因指皇后侍兒曰：「是皆我物。」

translations.literal: He then pointed at the empress's attendants and said: 'These are all my possessions.'
translations.idiomatic: He pointed at the empress's attendants and said: "These are all mine."

sentences.zh: 此言幾許異事。

translations.literal: These words—how many strange things!
translations.idiomatic: What extraordinary words these are.

sentences.zh: 其婦初亡，即以鬥帳安余老嫗。

translations.literal: When his consort first died, he immediately set up a canopy tent for an old woman named Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When his consort first died, he immediately installed an old woman named Yu in a canopy tent.

sentences.zh: 新婦初亡，我深疑使馬嗣明藥殺。

translations.literal: When the new bride first died, I deeply suspected he had Ma Siming poison her to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the new bride first died, I strongly suspected he had Ma Siming poison her.

sentences.zh: 我曾責之，便懟曰：「會殺元孝矩。」

translations.literal: I once reproached him, and he retorted: 'I will kill Yuan Xiaoju.'
translations.idiomatic: When I reproached him, he retorted: "I will kill Yuan Xiaoju."

sentences.zh: 此欲害我而遷怒耳。

translations.literal: This was wishing to harm me and venting anger elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to harm me and vented his anger elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 初，長寧誕育，朕與皇后共抱養之，自懷彼此，連遣來索。

translations.literal: At first, when Changning was born, the empress and I together nursed and raised him. Harboring partial feelings, Yong repeatedly sent people to demand him back.
translations.idiomatic: When Changning was born, the empress and I raised him together, but Yong, favoring his own side, repeatedly sent people to claim him.

sentences.zh: 且雲定興女，在外私合而生，想此由來，何必是其體胤！

translations.literal: Moreover, he is the daughter of Yun Dingxing, born from a secret union outside—considering this origin, why must he be Yong's own flesh and blood!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he is the daughter of Yun Dingxing, born of a secret liaison—given this origin, why must he be Yong's true son!

sentences.zh: 昔晉太子取屠家女，其兒即好屠割。

translations.literal: In former times the Jin crown prince took a butcher's daughter as wife, and his son immediately loved butchering and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Jin crown prince married a butcher's daughter, and his son took to butchering.

sentences.zh: 今儻非類，便亂宗社。

translations.literal: If now he is not of the proper kind, he will disrupt the ancestral temple and state.
translations.idiomatic: If he is not of the proper kind, he will ruin the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 又劉金驎諂佞人也，呼定興作親家翁，定興愚人，受其此語。

translations.literal: Moreover, Liu Jinlin is a flatterer and sycophant who calls Dingxing 'father-in-law.' Dingxing is a fool and accepts such words from him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jinlin is a flatterer who calls Dingxing "father-in-law," and the fool Dingxing accepts it.

sentences.zh: 我前解金驎者，為其此事。

translations.literal: The reason I previously dismissed Jinlin was for this matter.
translations.idiomatic: I dismissed Jinlin earlier for this very reason.

sentences.zh: 勇嘗引曹妙達共定興女同燕，妙達在外說雲：'我今得勸妃酒。」

translations.literal: Yong once brought Cao Miaoda to feast together with Dingxing's daughter. Miaoda spoke outside, saying: 'Today I was able to urge the consort to drink.'
translations.idiomatic: Yong once had Cao Miaoda feast with Dingxing's daughter; Miaoda boasted outside: "Today I got to urge the consort to drink."

sentences.zh: 直以其諸子偏庶，畏人不服，故逆縱之，欲收天下之望耳。

translations.literal: It is simply because his sons are all by concubines and he fears people will not submit that he deliberately indulges them, wishing to win the world's regard.
translations.idiomatic: He indulges them only because his sons are all by concubines and he fears people will not accept them—he seeks to win public favor.

sentences.zh: 我雖德慚堯、舜，終不以萬姓付不肖子也。

translations.literal: Although my virtue falls short of Yao and Shun, I will ultimately not entrust the myriad people to an unworthy son.
translations.idiomatic: Though my virtue falls short of Yao and Shun, I will never entrust the people to an unworthy son.

sentences.zh: 我恆畏其加害，如防大敵，今欲廢之，以安天下。」

translations.literal: I constantly fear he will harm me, guarding against him as against a great enemy. Now I wish to depose him to secure the realm."
translations.idiomatic: I have constantly feared his harm, guarding against him as against a great enemy; now I wish to depose him to secure the realm."

sentences.zh: 左衛大將軍、五原西元旻諫曰：「廢立大事，天子無二言，詔旨若行，後悔無及。

translations.literal: General of the Left Guard, Yuan Min of Wuyuan, remonstrated, saying: 'Deposition and installation are great matters. The Son of Heaven has no second word. If the edict is carried out, regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Left Guard Yuan Min of Wuyuan remonstrated: "Deposition and installation are grave matters; once the Son of Heaven speaks, there is no reversal. If this edict is carried out, regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 讒言罔極，惟陛下察之。」

translations.literal: Slander knows no limit—may Your Majesty examine it carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Slander knows no bounds—may Your Majesty examine it carefully.

sentences.zh: 旻辭直爭強，聲色俱厲，上不答。

translations.literal: Min's words were direct and contentious; his voice and expression were both fierce. The emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Min spoke bluntly and forcefully, his voice and expression fierce; the emperor did not answer.

sentences.zh: 是時姬威又抗表告太子非法。

translations.literal: At this time Ji Wei again submitted a memorial accusing the crown prince of illegal conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Ji Wei submitted another memorial accusing the crown prince of misconduct.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂威曰：「太子事蹟，宜皆盡言。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said to Wei: 'The crown prince's deeds—you should speak of them all fully.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen told Ji Wei: "Tell me everything about the crown prince's conduct.

sentences.zh: 威對曰：「皇太子由來共臣語，唯意在驕奢，欲得從樊川以至於散關，總規為苑。

translations.literal: Wei replied: 'The crown prince has always spoken with your subject, his mind set only on arrogance and extravagance. He wished to take from Fanchuan all the way to Sanguan Pass and plan the whole as an imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wei replied: "The crown prince has always told me he wanted to take land from Fanchuan to Sanguan Pass and turn it all into an imperial park.

sentences.zh: 兼雲：'昔漢武帝將起上林苑，東方朔諫之，賜朔黃金百斤，幾許可笑。

translations.literal: He also said: 'In former times when Emperor Wu of Han was about to build the Shanglin Park, Dongfang Shuo remonstrated and was given a hundred jin of gold—how laughable!'
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "When Emperor Wu of Han planned the Shanglin Park, Dongfang Shuo remonstrated and was given a hundred jin of gold—how ridiculous!"

sentences.zh: 我實無金輒賜此等。

translations.literal: I truly have no gold to bestow on such people.
translations.idiomatic: I have no gold to give such people.

sentences.zh: 若有諫者，正當斬之，不過殺百許人，自然永息。

translations.literal: If there are remonstrators, they should simply be beheaded—killing no more than a hundred or so people, and naturally all will cease forever.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone remonstrates, they should simply be beheaded—kill a hundred or so and the matter will end forever.

sentences.zh: '前蘇孝慈解左衛率，皇太子奮髯揚肘曰：'大丈夫會當有一日，終不忘之，決當快意。

translations.literal: Previously when Su Xiaoci was dismissed from Left Guard Commander, the crown prince bristled his beard and raised his elbow, saying: 'A real man will surely have his day—I will never forget this and will certainly have my satisfaction.'
translations.idiomatic: When Su Xiaoci was dismissed as Left Guard Commander, the crown prince bristled and said: "A real man will have his day—I will never forget this and will have my revenge.'

sentences.zh: '又宮內所須，尚書多執法不與，便怒曰：'僕射以下，吾會戮一二人，使知慢我之禍。

translations.literal: Moreover, for what the inner palace needed, the Ministry of State Affairs often enforced the law and refused to provide them. He angrily said: 'From the Vice Director down, I will kill one or two to let them know the disaster of slighting me.'
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of State Affairs refused palace requisitions on legal grounds, he raged: "From the Vice Director down, I will kill one or two to teach them the cost of slighting me.'

sentences.zh: '又于苑內築一小城，春夏秋冬，作役不輟，營起亭殿，朝造夕改。

translations.literal: He also built a small city within the park; spring, summer, autumn, and winter, labor never ceased. Pavilions and halls were constructed, built in the morning and altered by evening.
translations.idiomatic: He also built a small city in the park where labor never ceased through the seasons, erecting pavilions and halls that were built in the morning and changed by evening.

sentences.zh: 每雲：'至尊嗔我多側庶，高緯、陳叔寶豈是孽子乎？

translations.literal: He often said: 'The Supreme One blames me for having many sons by concubines—were Gao Wei and Chen Shubao illegitimate sons?'
translations.idiomatic: He often said: "The emperor blames me for having many sons by concubines—were Gao Wei and Chen Shubao illegitimate sons?'

sentences.zh: '嘗令師姥卜吉凶，語臣曰：'至尊忌在十八年，此期促矣。

translations.literal: He once had a divining matron read fortunes and told your subject: 'The Supreme One's taboo falls in the eighteenth year—this deadline is approaching.'
translations.idiomatic: He once had a diviner read fortunes and told me: "The emperor's fate falls in the eighteenth year— that deadline is near.'

sentences.zh: '」高祖泫然曰：「誰非父母生，乃至於此！

translations.literal: Gaozu said with tears: 'Who is not born of parents—yet it has come to this!'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said tearfully: "Who is not born of parents—yet it has come to this!"

sentences.zh: 我有舊使婦女，令看東宮，奏我雲：'勿令廣平王至皇太子處。

translations.literal: I had an old serving woman watch the Eastern Palace. She reported to me: 'Do not let the Prince of Guangping go to the crown prince's place.'
translations.idiomatic: I had an old serving woman watch the Eastern Palace; she reported: "Do not let the Prince of Guangping go to the crown prince."

sentences.zh: 東宮憎婦，亦廣平教之。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace hates women—it was Guangping who taught this.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince hates women—it was Guangping who taught him this.

sentences.zh: '元贊亦知其陰惡，勸我于左藏之東，加置兩隊。

translations.literal: Yuan Zan also knew of his secret wickedness and urged me to add two guard units east of the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zan also knew of his secret wickedness and urged me to add two guard units east of the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 初平陳後，宮人好者悉配春坊，如聞不知厭足，於外更有求訪。

translations.literal: After the initial pacification of Chen, all the attractive palace women were assigned to the Spring Palace. I hear he is not satisfied and seeks more outside.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Chen, the best palace women were assigned to the Eastern Palace; I hear he is not satisfied and seeks more outside.

sentences.zh: 朕近覽《齊書》，見高歡縱其兒子，不勝忿憤，安可效尤邪！」

translations.literal: I recently read the Book of Qi and saw how Gao Huan indulged his son—I could not contain my anger. How could I follow such an example!'
translations.idiomatic: I recently read the Book of Qi and saw how Gao Huan indulged his son—I was furious; how could I follow such an example!"

sentences.zh: 於是勇及諸子皆被禁錮，部分收其黨與。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yong and all his sons were placed under confinement, and his partisans were partially arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and all his sons were then confined, and his associates were arrested.

sentences.zh: 楊素舞文巧詆，鍛煉以成其獄。

translations.literal: Yang Su twisted the law with cunning slander and forged evidence to complete the case.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su twisted the law with cunning accusations and forged evidence to complete the case.

sentences.zh: 勇由是遂敗。

translations.literal: Yong was thereby ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was thereby ruined.

sentences.zh: 居數日，有司承素意，奏言左衛元旻身備宿衛，常曲事於勇，情存附托，在仁壽宮，裴弘將勇書於朝堂與旻，題封雲勿令人見。

translations.literal: After several days, the responsible offices, following Su's intent, memorialized that Left Guard Yuan Min, being on night watch duty, constantly curried favor with Yong and harbored attachment to him. At Renshou Palace, Pei Hong brought Yong's letter in the court hall to Min; the sealed cover read 'Do not let anyone see.'
translations.idiomatic: Several days later, following Yang Su's lead, officials reported that Left Guard Yuan Min, on night watch duty, curried favor with Yong; at Renshou Palace, Pei Hong delivered Yong's letter to Min in the court hall with a seal reading "Do not let anyone see."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「朕在仁壽宮，有纖小事，東宮必知，疾于驛馬。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: 'When I am at Renshou Palace, even the slightest matter—the Eastern Palace always knows of it, faster than relay horses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said: "When I am at Renshou Palace, even the smallest matter reaches the Eastern Palace faster than relay horses.

sentences.zh: 怪之甚久，豈非此徒耶？」

translations.literal: I have wondered about this for a long time—is it not these people?
translations.idiomatic: I have wondered about this for a long time—is it not these people?

sentences.zh: 遣武士執旻及弘付法治其罪。

translations.literal: He dispatched warriors to seize Min and Hong and hand them over to the law to punish their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He sent warriors to arrest Min and Hong and hand them over for punishment.

sentences.zh: 先是，勇嘗從仁壽宮參起居還，途中見一枯槐，根幹蟠錯，大且五六圍，顧左右曰：「此堪作何器用？」

translations.literal: Earlier, Yong once returned from paying respects at Renshou Palace and on the way saw a withered pagoda tree, its roots and trunk tangled and twisted, five or six arm-spans around. He turned to those at his side and said: 'What sort of implement could this be made into?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, returning from paying respects at Renshou Palace, Yong saw a withered pagoda tree five or six arm-spans around and asked his attendants: "What could this be made into?

sentences.zh: 或對曰：「古槐尤堪取火。」

translations.literal: Someone replied: 'Ancient pagoda wood is especially good for fire-striking.'
translations.idiomatic: Someone replied: "Ancient pagoda wood is especially good for fire-striking."

sentences.zh: 于時衛士皆佩火燧，勇因令匠者造數千枚，欲以分賜左右。

translations.literal: At that time the guards all carried fire-strikers. Yong therefore ordered craftsmen to make several thousand and intended to distribute them to those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The guards all carried fire-strikers at the time, so Yong ordered craftsmen to make several thousand to distribute to his attendants.

sentences.zh: 至是，獲於庫。

translations.literal: At this point they were seized in the storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: They were now found in the storehouse.

sentences.zh: 又藥藏局貯艾數斛，亦搜得之。

translations.literal: Moreover, several hu of mugwort stored in the Medical Storehouse Bureau were also found in the search.
translations.idiomatic: Several hu of mugwort stored in the Medical Storehouse were also found.

sentences.zh: 大將為怪，以問姬威。

translations.literal: The general found it strange and questioned Ji Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The general found this suspicious and questioned Ji Wei.

sentences.zh: 威曰：「太子此意別有所在。

translations.literal: Wei said: 'The crown prince's intent in this has another purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wei said: "The crown prince had another purpose in this.

sentences.zh: 比令長寧王已下，詣仁壽宮還，每嘗急行，一宿便至。

translations.literal: Recently he ordered the Prince of Changning and those below to go to Renshou Palace and return, each time traveling urgently so they arrived in one night's rest.
translations.idiomatic: Recently he ordered the Prince of Changning and the others to go to Renshou Palace and return at full speed, arriving in a single night.

sentences.zh: 恆飼馬千匹，雲徑往捉城門，自然餓死。」

translations.literal: He constantly kept a thousand horses, saying they would go straight to seize the city gates and naturally starve the emperor to death.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a thousand horses at the ready, saying they would ride straight to seize the city gates and starve the emperor to death.

sentences.zh: 素以威言詰勇，勇不服曰：「竊聞公家馬數萬匹，勇忝備位太子，有馬千匹，乃是反乎？」

translations.literal: Su used Wei's words to interrogate Yong. Yong refused to accept it, saying: 'I have heard the government has tens of thousands of horses. Yong, though unworthy in the position of crown prince, has a thousand horses—is this rebellion?'
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su confronted Yong with Ji's accusation; Yong protested: "I hear the government has tens of thousands of horses—I, as crown prince, have a thousand; is that rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 素又發洩東宮服玩，似加周飾者，悉陳之於庭，以示文武群官，為太子之罪。

translations.literal: Su also brought out the Eastern Palace's garments and playthings, those that seemed excessively ornate, and displayed them all in the courtyard to show the civil and military officials as evidence of the crown prince's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su also brought out the Eastern Palace's lavish garments and ornaments and displayed them in the courtyard before civil and military officials as evidence of the crown prince's crimes.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣將諸物示勇，以誚詰之。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent people to bring the various items to show Yong and reproach and interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent the items to Yong to confront and reproach him.

sentences.zh: 皇后又責之罪。

translations.literal: The empress also reproached him for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The empress also reproached him for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 高祖使使責問勇，勇不服。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent emissaries to reproach and question Yong; Yong refused to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent envoys to question Yong; Yong denied the charges.

sentences.zh: 太史令袁充進曰：「臣觀天文，皇太子當廢。」

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Astronomical Bureau Yuan Chong stepped forward and said: 'Your subject observes the heavens—the crown prince should be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Astronomical Bureau Yuan Chong stepped forward: "I observe the heavens—the crown prince should be deposed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「玄象久見矣，群臣無敢言者。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'The celestial signs have long been visible, yet none of the ministers dared speak.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The celestial signs have long been visible, yet no minister dared speak."

sentences.zh: 於是使人召勇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent someone to summon Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent for Yong.

sentences.zh: 勇見使者，驚曰：「得無殺我耶？」

translations.literal: When Yong saw the emissary, he startled and said: 'Surely they are not going to kill me?
translations.idiomatic: When Yong saw the envoy, he startled and said: "Are they going to kill me?

sentences.zh: 高祖戎服陳兵，禦武德殿，集百官，立于東面，諸親立於西面，引勇及諸子列於殿庭。

translations.literal: Gaozu, in military dress with troops arrayed, presided at Wude Hall, assembled the hundred officials standing on the east side and the princes on the west, and led Yong and his sons to stand in ranks in the hall courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, in military dress with troops arrayed, presided at Wude Hall; officials stood on the east, princes on the west, and Yong and his sons were brought before the hall.

sentences.zh: 命薛道衡宣廢勇之詔曰：「太子之位，實為國本，苟非其人，不可虛立。

translations.literal: He ordered Xue Daoheng to proclaim the edict deposing Yong, saying: 'The position of crown prince is truly the foundation of the state. If the person is not suitable, the post cannot be vacantly established.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xue Daoheng to proclaim the edict deposing Yong: "The crown prince is the foundation of the state; if the person is unfit, the post cannot be held in vain.

sentences.zh: 自古儲副，或有不才，長惡不悛，仍令守器，皆由情溺寵愛，失於至理，致使宗社傾亡，蒼生塗地。

translations.literal: Since ancient times among heirs apparent, some have lacked talent, persisted in evil without reform, yet were still allowed to hold the vessel—all because affection drowned in favoritism, losing the supreme principle, causing the ancestral temple and state to topple and the common people to be trampled.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout history, unfit heirs who persisted in evil yet retained the succession did so only because rulers indulged affection over reason, bringing down dynasties and ruining the people.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，天下安危，系乎上嗣，大業傳世，豈不重哉！

translations.literal: Speaking from this, the safety and peril of the realm depend on the supreme heir. The great enterprise passed down through generations—how could it not be weighty!
translations.idiomatic: The safety of the realm depends on the heir—the succession is no light matter!

sentences.zh: 皇太子勇，地則居長，情所鍾愛，初登大位，即建春宮，冀德業日新，隆茲負荷。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong, by position the eldest and in affection deeply cherished, when I first ascended the throne immediately established the Eastern Palace, hoping his virtue and achievements would daily renew and elevate this burden he bears.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong, the eldest and deeply cherished, was made heir when I first took the throne, in hope that his virtue would grow daily and he would bear this weight well.

sentences.zh: 而性識庸暗，仁孝無聞，昵近小人，委任奸佞，前後愆釁，難以具紀。

translations.literal: Yet his nature and understanding are mediocre and dim; benevolence and filial piety are unheard of; he draws close to petty men and entrusts affairs to the wicked. His offenses before and after are too numerous to record in full.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he is dull of mind, devoid of benevolence and filial piety, consorts with petty men and trusts the wicked—his offenses are too numerous to record.

sentences.zh: 但百姓者，天之百姓，朕恭天命，屬當安育，雖欲愛子，實畏上靈，豈敢以不肖之子而亂天下。

translations.literal: But the common people are Heaven's common people. I respectfully receive Heaven's mandate and am charged with nurturing them in peace. Though I wish to love my son, I truly fear the Supreme Spirit—how could I dare use an unworthy son to disrupt the realm?
translations.idiomatic: The people belong to Heaven; I receive Heaven's mandate to nurture them in peace. Though I love my son, I fear Heaven—how could I let an unworthy son disrupt the realm?

sentences.zh: 勇及其男女為王、公主者，並可廢為庶人。

translations.literal: Yong and his sons and daughters who hold the titles of king and princess are all to be deposed and made commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and his sons and daughters who hold princely and princess titles are all deposed to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 顧惟兆庶，事不獲已，歎言及此，良深愧歎！」

translations.literal: Considering the myriad people, the matter cannot be avoided. Sighing to speak of this, I am deeply ashamed and grieved!
translations.idiomatic: For the sake of the people the matter cannot be avoided—I sigh with deep shame and grief!

sentences.zh: 令薛道衡謂勇曰：「爾之罪惡，人神所棄，欲求不廢，其可得耶？」

translations.literal: He ordered Xue Daoheng to tell Yong: 'Your crimes are abandoned by men and spirits. To seek not to be deposed—can that be obtained?'
translations.idiomatic: Xue Daoheng told Yong: "Your crimes are abandoned by men and spirits—can you hope to avoid deposition?"

sentences.zh: 勇再拜而言曰：「臣合屍之都市，為將來鑒誡，幸蒙哀憐，得全性命。」

translations.literal: Yong bowed twice and said: 'Your subject deserves to leave his corpse in the market as a warning for the future. Fortunately receiving compassionate pity, I preserve my life.'
translations.idiomatic: Yong bowed twice and said: "I deserve to die in the marketplace as a warning to future generations; I am grateful to be spared my life."

sentences.zh: 言畢，泣下流襟，既而舞蹈而去。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking, tears streamed down his collar; then he performed the dance of obeisance and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished, tears streamed down his robe; he performed the obeisance dance and departed.

sentences.zh: 左右莫不憫默。

translations.literal: Those at his side were all silent in pity.
translations.idiomatic: All present were silent in pity.

sentences.zh: 又下詔曰：

translations.literal: Another edict was also issued, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Another edict was issued:

sentences.zh: :自古以來，朝危國亂，皆邪臣佞媚，凶黨扇惑，致使禍及宗社，毒流兆庶。

translations.literal: Since ancient times, when the court was endangered and the state in turmoil, it was always because wicked ministers flattered and fawned and evil factions incited confusion, causing disaster to reach the ancestral temple and state and poison to flow to the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: Since ancient times, court crises and national turmoil have always been caused by wicked ministers who flattered and evil factions who incited confusion, bringing disaster to the state and harm to the people.

sentences.zh: 若不標明典憲，何以肅清天下！

translations.literal: If the canonical laws are not clearly proclaimed, how can the realm be purged and cleared!
translations.idiomatic: If the law is not clearly proclaimed, how can the realm be purged!

sentences.zh: 左衛大將軍、五原郡西元旻，任掌兵衛，委以心膂，陪侍左右，恩寵隆渥，乃包藏奸伏，離間君親，崇長厲階，最為魁首。

translations.literal: General of the Left Guard, Yuan Min of Wuyuan Commandery, charged with military guard duty, entrusted as heart and backbone, attending at left and right with abundant favor and grace—yet he harbored treachery in secret, sowed discord between ruler and kin, encouraged and lengthened the steps of evil, and was foremost among the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Left Guard Yuan Min of Wuyuan, entrusted with military guard duty and favored at court, harbored treachery, sowed discord between ruler and kin, and was foremost among the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 太子左庶子唐令則，策名儲貳，位長宮僚，諂曲取容，音技自進，躬執樂器，親教內人，贊成驕侈，導引非法。

translations.literal: Left Assistant to the Crown Prince Tang Lingze, registered in the heir's service and chief among palace officials, flattered and curried favor, advanced himself through music and skill, personally wielded instruments and directly taught inner women, abetted arrogance and extravagance, and led into unlawful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant to the Crown Prince Tang Lingze, chief among palace officials, flattered for favor, advanced himself through music, personally taught palace women, and abetted extravagance and unlawful conduct.

sentences.zh: 太子家令鄒文騰，專行左道，偏被親昵，心腹委付，巨細關知，占問國家，希覬災禍。

translations.literal: Household Steward of the Crown Prince Zou Wenteng practiced heterodox ways exclusively, was especially favored and intimate, entrusted as confidant knowing all great and small matters, divined about the state, and hoped for calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Household Steward of the Crown Prince Zou Wenteng practiced heterodox ways, was especially favored as a confidant privy to all matters, divined about the state, and hoped for calamity.

sentences.zh: 左衛率司馬夏侯福，內事諂諛，外作威勢，淩侮上下，褻濁宮闈。

translations.literal: Major of the Left Guard Commander Xiahou Fu flattered within and displayed power without, insulting superiors and inferiors and defiling the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Major of the Left Guard Commander Xiahou Fu flattered within and bullied without, insulting all ranks and defiling the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 典膳監元淹，謬陳愛憎，開示怨隙，妄起訕謗，潛行離阻，進引妖巫，營事厭禱。

translations.literal: Director of Palace Provisions Yuan Yan wrongly expressed likes and dislikes, opened and revealed grievances, groundlessly raised slander, secretly carried out separation and obstruction, introduced sorcerers and witches, and conducted apotropaic rites.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Palace Provisions Yuan Yan expressed partiality, stirred up grievances, spread slander, sowed division, introduced sorcerers, and conducted apotropaic rites.

sentences.zh: 前吏部侍郎蕭子寶，往居省閣，舊非宮臣，稟性浮躁，用懷輕險，進畫奸謀，要射榮利，經營間構，開造禍端。

translations.literal: Former Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Xiao Zibao, who formerly served in the ministry offices and was not originally a palace official, was by nature restless and harbored reckless danger, advancing wicked plots, seeking glory and profit, scheming to sow discord and opening the source of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Former Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Xiao Zibao, not originally a palace official, was restless by nature and advanced wicked plots for personal gain, scheming to sow discord and open the way to disaster.

sentences.zh: 前主璽下士何竦，假託玄象，妄說妖怪，志圖禍亂，心在速發，兼制奇器異服，皆竦規摹，增長驕奢，糜費百姓。

translations.literal: Former Seal Keeper Attendant He Song falsely invoked celestial signs, groundlessly spoke of demons and monsters, intended to plot turmoil, with his heart set on quick action. He also made strange implements and unusual garments—all Song's designs—increasing arrogance and extravagance and wasting the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Former Seal Keeper Attendant He Song falsely invoked celestial signs, spoke groundlessly of omens, plotted turmoil with haste in mind, and made strange implements and garments of his own design, increasing extravagance and wasting the people's resources.

sentences.zh: 凡此七人，為害乃甚，並處斬，妻妾子孫皆悉沒官。

translations.literal: All these seven men caused great harm and were all executed; their wives, concubines, and descendants were all confiscated as government property.
translations.idiomatic: All seven of these men had caused great harm and were executed; their wives, concubines, and descendants were all confiscated.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍閻毗、東郡公崔君綽、游騎尉沈福寶、瀛州民章仇太翼等四人，所為之事，皆是悖惡，論其狀跡，罪合極刑。

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Yan Pi, Duke of Dongjun Cui Junchuo, Cavalry Commandant Shen Fubao, and Zhangqiu Taiyi, a commoner of Yingzhou—their deeds were all rebellious and wicked. Judging their conduct and traces, their crimes merited capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: General of Chariots and Cavalry Yan Pi, Duke of Dongjun Cui Junchuo, Cavalry Commandant Shen Fubao, and Zhangqiu Taiyi of Yingzhou had all committed wicked deeds meriting capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 但朕情存好生，未能盡戮，可並特免死，各決杖一百，身及妻子資財田宅，悉可沒官。

translations.literal: But I cherish life and could not execute them all. They are all specially spared death, each to receive a hundred blows with the rod. Their persons, wives, children, property, and estates may all be confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: But I cherish life and could not execute them all; they are spared death but each receives a hundred blows with the rod, and their persons, families, property, and estates are confiscated.

sentences.zh: 副將作大匠高龍義，豫追番丁，輒配東宮使役，營造亭舍，進入春坊。

translations.literal: Assistant Master of Palace Construction Gao Longyi, in advance requisitioned corvée laborers and immediately assigned them to the Eastern Palace for service, constructing pavilions and lodges that entered the Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Master of Palace Construction Gao Longyi requisitioned corvée laborers in advance and assigned them to the Eastern Palace to build pavilions and lodges.

sentences.zh: 率更令晉文建，通直散騎侍郎、判司農少卿事元衡，料度之外，私自出給，虛破丁功，擅割園地。

translations.literal: Director of the Water Clock Jin Wenjian and Attendant Cavalier Yuan Heng, acting Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, beyond their estimates privately issued supplies, falsely depleted corvée labor, and arbitrarily seized garden land.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Water Clock Jin Wenjian and Attendant Cavalier Yuan Heng, acting Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, issued supplies beyond their estimates, falsely depleted corvée labor, and seized garden land.

sentences.zh: 並處盡。

translations.literal: All were executed.
translations.idiomatic: All were executed.

sentences.zh: 於是集群官于廣陽門外，宣詔以戮之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the assembled officials were gathered outside Guangyang Gate, and the edict was proclaimed as they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were then assembled outside Guangyang Gate and the edict was proclaimed as the sentences were carried out.

sentences.zh: 廣平王雄答詔曰：「至尊為百姓割骨肉之恩，廢黜無德，實為大慶，天下幸甚！」

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangping, Xiong, replied to the edict: 'The Supreme One has severed flesh-and-blood ties for the sake of the common people and deposed the unworthy—this is truly a great celebration; the realm is greatly fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangping Xiong replied to the edict: "Your Majesty has severed flesh-and-blood ties for the people's sake and deposed the unworthy—this is a great blessing for the realm!

sentences.zh: 乃移勇於內史省，立晉王廣為皇太子，仍以勇付之，複囚於東宮。

translations.literal: Yong was then moved to the Inner Scribe Directorate. The Prince of Jin, Guang, was installed as crown prince, and Yong was still handed over to him and again imprisoned in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was moved to the Inner Scribe Directorate; the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, was made crown prince, and Yong was handed over to him and imprisoned again in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 賜楊素物三千段，元胄、楊約並千段，楊難敵五百段，皆鞫勇之功賞也。

translations.literal: Yang Su was granted three thousand bolts of goods; Yuan Zhou and Yang Yue each a thousand bolts; Yang Nandi five hundred bolts—all rewards for their merit in prosecuting Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su was granted three thousand bolts of goods; Yuan Zhou and Yang Yue each a thousand; Yang Nandi five hundred—all rewards for prosecuting Yong.

sentences.zh: 時文林郎楊孝政上書諫曰：「皇太子為小人所誤，宜加訓誨，不宜廢黜。」

translations.literal: At that time Palace Scholar Yang Xiaozheng submitted a memorial remonstrating: 'The crown prince was misled by petty men—he should be further instructed and admonished, not deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Scholar Yang Xiaozheng submitted a memorial: "The crown prince was misled by petty men—he should be instructed, not deposed.

sentences.zh: 上怒，撻其胸。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and struck his chest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and struck him on the chest.

sentences.zh: 尋而貝州長史裴肅表稱：「庶人罪黜已久，當克己自新，請封一小國。」

translations.literal: Soon afterward Chief Administrator of Beizhou Pei Su submitted a memorial saying: 'The commoner has been punished and deposed for a long time; he should restrain himself and reform. I request he be enfeoffed with a small state.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chief Administrator of Beizhou Pei Su submitted a memorial: "The deposed prince has long been punished; he should reform himself—I request he be enfeoffed with a small state.

sentences.zh: 高祖知勇之黜也，不允天下之情，乃征肅入朝，具陳廢立之意。

translations.literal: Gaozu knew that Yong's deposition did not accord with the feelings of the realm. He therefore summoned Su to court and fully set forth the reasons for deposition and installation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen knew Yong's deposition did not satisfy public sentiment; he summoned Pei Su to court and fully explained the reasons for the deposition.

sentences.zh: 時勇自以廢非其罪，頻請見上，面申冤屈。

translations.literal: At that time Yong himself believed his deposition was not for his crimes and repeatedly requested an audience with the emperor to state his grievances in person.
translations.idiomatic: Yong believed his deposition was unjust and repeatedly requested an audience to plead his case in person.

sentences.zh: 而皇太子遏之，不得聞奏。

translations.literal: But the crown prince blocked him, and his petitions could not reach the throne.
translations.idiomatic: But the crown prince blocked him and his petitions never reached the emperor.

sentences.zh: 勇於是升樹大叫，聲聞于上，冀得引見。

translations.literal: Yong thereupon climbed a tree and shouted loudly, his voice reaching the emperor above, hoping to be summoned for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Yong climbed a tree and shouted loudly, hoping his voice would reach the emperor and win him an audience.

sentences.zh: 素因奏言：「勇情志昏亂，為癲鬼所著，不可複收。」

translations.literal: Su thereupon memorialized: 'Yong's mind and emotions are confused and disordered; he is possessed by a mad demon and cannot be taken back.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su memorialized: "Yong's mind is deranged—he is possessed by madness and cannot be restored.

sentences.zh: 上以為然，卒不得見。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct, and Yong ultimately could not obtain an audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and Yong never obtained an audience.

sentences.zh: 素誣陷經營，構成其罪，類皆如此。

translations.literal: Su's fabrications and entrapments, constructing his crimes, were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su's fabrications and frame-ups were all of this sort.

sentences.zh: 高祖寢疾于仁壽宮，征皇太子入侍醫藥，而奸亂宮闈，事聞于高祖。

translations.literal: Gaozu fell ill at Renshou Palace and summoned the crown prince to attend him with medicine, but misconduct in the inner palace reached Gaozu's ears.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen fell ill at Renshou Palace and summoned the crown prince to attend him, but misconduct in the inner palace reached his ears.

sentences.zh: 高祖抵床曰：「枉廢我兒！」

translations.literal: Gaozu struck the bed and said: 'I wrongly deposed my son!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen struck the bed and cried: "I wrongly deposed my son!

sentences.zh: 因遣追勇。

translations.literal: He thereupon dispatched orders to recall Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He sent orders to recall Yong.

sentences.zh: 未及發使，高祖暴崩，秘不發喪。

translations.literal: Before the emissary could be sent, Gaozu suddenly died. The death was kept secret and mourning was not announced.
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoy could be sent, Emperor Wen suddenly died; the death was kept secret.

sentences.zh: 遽收柳述、元岩，系於大理獄，偽為高祖敕書，賜庶人死。

translations.literal: Liu Shu and Yuan Yan were hastily arrested and imprisoned in the Court of Judicial Review. A forged edict in Gaozu's name was issued, granting death to the commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shu and Yuan Yan were hastily arrested and imprisoned; a forged edict in the late emperor's name ordered Yong's death.

sentences.zh: 追封房陵王，不為立嗣。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Fangling, but no heir was established.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Fangling, but no heir was established.

sentences.zh: 勇有十男：雲昭訓生長寧王儼、平原王裕、安城王筠，高良娣生安平王嶷、襄城王恪，王良媛生高陽王該、建安王韶，成姬生潁川王煚，後宮生孝實、孝範。

translations.literal: Yong had ten sons: Lady Yun Zhaoxun bore the Prince of Changning Yan, Prince of Pingyuan Yu, and Prince of Ancheng Jun; Lady Gao bore the Prince of Anping Ni and Prince of Xiangcheng Ke; Lady Wang bore the Prince of Gaoyang Gai and Prince of Jian'an Shao; Lady Cheng bore the Prince of Yingchuan Jiong; the rear palace bore Xiaoshi and Xiaofan.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had ten sons: Lady Yun Zhaoxun bore the Princes of Changning (Yan), Pingyuan (Yu), and Ancheng (Jun); Lady Gao bore the Princes of Anping (Ni) and Xiangcheng (Ke); Lady Wang bore the Princes of Gaoyang (Gai) and Jian'an (Shao); Lady Cheng bore the Prince of Yingchuan (Jiong); and the rear palace bore Xiaoshi and Xiaofan.

sentences.zh: 長寧王儼，勇長子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changning, Yan, was Yong's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changning, Yan, was Yong's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 誕乳之初，以報高祖，高祖曰：「此即皇太孫，何乃生不得地？」

translations.literal: At the first report of his birth and nursing, Gaozu was informed. Gaozu said: 'This is the imperial great-grandson—why was he born without proper place?
translations.idiomatic: When his birth was reported, Emperor Wen said: "This is the imperial great-grandson—why was he born in an improper place?

sentences.zh: 雲定興奏曰：「天生龍種，所以因雲而出。」

translations.literal: Yun Dingxing memorialized: 'Heaven-born dragon seed—therefore he emerged with the clouds.'
translations.idiomatic: Yun Dingxing replied: "Heaven-born dragon seed—therefore he emerged with the clouds."

sentences.zh: 時人以為敏對。

translations.literal: People of the time considered this a quick-witted reply.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time considered this a clever reply.

sentences.zh: 六歲，封長寧郡王。

translations.literal: At six years of age he was enfeoffed as Prince of Changning Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At six he was enfeoffed as Prince of Changning.

sentences.zh: 勇敗，亦坐廢黜。

translations.literal: When Yong was ruined, he was also deposed by association.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong fell, he was deposed as well.

sentences.zh: 上表乞宿衛，辭情哀切，高祖覽而憫焉。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial begging for night watch duty; his words were mournful and earnest. Gaozu read it and pitied him.
