translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial begging for palace guard duty; his words were mournful and earnest, and Emperor Wen pitied him.

sentences.zh: 楊素進曰：「伏願聖心同於螫手，不宜複留意。」

translations.literal: Yang Su stepped forward and said: 'I humbly wish Your Majesty's heart would be like one stung by a scorpion—You should not again take notice of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su stepped forward: "I humbly wish Your Majesty's heart would be like one stung by a scorpion—you should not take notice of him again.

sentences.zh: 煬帝踐極，儼常從行，卒於道，實鴆之也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Yan often accompanied him on travels and died on the road—it was in fact poison.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Yan often accompanied him on travels and died on the road—he was in fact poisoned.

sentences.zh: 諸弟分徙嶺外，仍敕在所皆殺焉。

translations.literal: His younger brothers were separately exiled beyond the mountain ranges, and orders were still issued that all be killed wherever they were.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers were exiled beyond the mountains, and orders were issued that all be killed wherever they were.

sentences.zh: 秦孝王俊，字阿祗，高祖第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xiao of Qin, Yang Jun, courtesy name Azhi, was the third son of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun, Prince Xiao of Qin, whose courtesy name was Azhi, was the third son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年立為秦王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang, he was established as Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang, he was made Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 二年春，拜上柱國、河南道行台尚書令、洛州刺史，時年十二。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he was appointed Grand Preceptor of State, Director of the Henan Circuit Executive and Minister of State Affairs, and Governor of Luozhou—he was then twelve years old.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year he was appointed Grand Preceptor of State, Director of the Henan Circuit Executive, and Governor of Luozhou—he was twelve years old.

sentences.zh: 加右武衛大將軍，領關東兵。

translations.literal: He was additionally made General of the Right Martial Guard and put in charge of the eastern pass troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made General of the Right Martial Guard and put in charge of the eastern pass troops.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷秦州總管。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Governor-General of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Governor-General of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 隴右諸州盡隸焉。

translations.literal: All the prefectures of Longyou were placed under his authority.
translations.idiomatic: All the prefectures of Longyou were placed under his authority.

sentences.zh: 俊仁恕慈愛，崇敬佛道，請為沙門，上不許。

translations.literal: Jun was benevolent, forgiving, and compassionate, revered Buddhism and Daoism, and requested to become a monk—the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was benevolent and compassionate, revered Buddhism and Daoism, and requested to become a monk—the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷山南道行台尚書令。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Director of the Shannan Circuit Executive and Minister of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to Director of the Shannan Circuit Executive.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之役，以為山南道行軍元帥，督三十總管，水陸十余萬，屯漢口，為上流節度。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen he served as campaign commander of the Shannan Circuit, supervising thirty governor-generals with more than a hundred thousand troops by land and water, encamped at Hankou as commander of the upper stream.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Chen he served as campaign commander of the Shannan Circuit, supervising thirty governor-generals with more than a hundred thousand troops by land and water, encamped at Hankou commanding the upper stream.

sentences.zh: 陳將周羅睺、荀法尚等，以勁兵數萬屯鸚鵡洲，總管崔弘度請擊之。

translations.literal: The Chen generals Zhou Luohou, Xun Fashang, and others encamped with tens of thousands of elite troops at Parrot Isle. Governor-General Cui Hongdu requested to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen generals Zhou Luohou and Xun Fashang encamped with tens of thousands of elite troops at Parrot Isle; Governor-General Cui Hongdu requested to attack.

sentences.zh: 俊慮殺傷，不許。

translations.literal: Jun, concerned about killing and wounding, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, concerned about casualties, refused.

sentences.zh: 羅睺亦相率而降。

translations.literal: Luohou also led his men in surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou then led his men in surrender.

sentences.zh: 於是遣使奉章詣闕，垂泣謂使者曰：「謬當推轂，愧無尺寸之功，以此多慚耳。」

translations.literal: He thereupon sent an emissary to submit a memorial to the throne and said through tears to the envoy: 'I was wrongly placed in command and am ashamed to have achieved not even an inch of merit—this is why I am deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent an emissary to submit a memorial to the throne and said through tears: "I was wrongly placed in command and am ashamed to have achieved no merit at all.

sentences.zh: 上聞而善之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of this and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of this and approved.

sentences.zh: 授揚州總管四十四州諸軍事，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor-General of Yangzhou over forty-four prefectures and all military affairs, stationed at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor-General of Yangzhou over forty-four prefectures, stationed at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉并州總管二十四州諸軍事。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Governor-General of Bingzhou over twenty-four prefectures and all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was transferred to Governor-General of Bingzhou over twenty-four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 初頗有令問，高祖聞而大悅，下書獎勵焉。

translations.literal: At first he had quite a good reputation. Gaozu heard of this and was greatly pleased, issuing a letter of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: At first he had a good reputation; Emperor Wen was greatly pleased and issued a letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 其後俊漸奢侈，違犯制度，出錢求息，民吏苦之。

translations.literal: Afterward Jun gradually became extravagant, violated regulations, lent money for interest, and the people and officials suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jun grew extravagant, violated regulations, lent money at interest, and the people and officials suffered.

sentences.zh: 上遣使按其事，與相連坐者百餘人。

translations.literal: The emperor sent emissaries to investigate the matter; more than a hundred people were implicated by association.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent officials to investigate; more than a hundred people were implicated.

sentences.zh: 俊猶不悛，於是盛治宮室，窮極侈麗。

translations.literal: Jun still did not reform. Thereupon he lavishly built palaces and halls to the utmost extravagance and splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Jun still did not reform and lavishly built palaces to the utmost extravagance.

sentences.zh: 俊有巧思，每親運斤斧，工巧之器，飾以珠玉。

translations.literal: Jun had clever ideas and personally wielded axe and adze, making ingenious implements ornamented with pearls and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was clever with his hands and personally wielded tools, making ingenious implements ornamented with pearls and jade.

sentences.zh: 為妃作七寶羃籬，又為水殿，香塗粉壁，玉砌金階。

translations.literal: For his consort he made a seven-jewel canopy screen, and also a water palace with fragrant plaster and powdered walls, jade steps and golden stairs.
translations.idiomatic: For his consort he made a seven-jewel canopy screen and a water palace with fragrant plaster, powdered walls, jade steps, and golden stairs.

sentences.zh: 樑柱楣棟之間，周以明鏡，間以寶珠，極榮飾之美。

translations.literal: Between beams, pillars, lintels, and rafters, bright mirrors were placed all around, interspersed with pearls—beauty of ornament taken to the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Between beams, pillars, and rafters he placed bright mirrors interspersed with pearls—ornament taken to the extreme.

sentences.zh: 每與賓客妓女弦歌于其上。

translations.literal: He often feasted with guests and courtesans, playing stringed instruments and singing upon it.
translations.idiomatic: He often feasted with guests and courtesans there, playing music and singing.

sentences.zh: 俊頗好內，妃崔氏性妒，甚不平之，遂於瓜中進毒。

translations.literal: Jun was quite fond of women. His consort Lady Cui was jealous and greatly resentful, and thereupon placed poison in a melon.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was fond of women; his consort Lady Cui was jealous and placed poison in a melon.

sentences.zh: 俊由是遇疾，征還京師。

translations.literal: Jun thereby fell ill and was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jun fell ill and was summoned back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上以其奢縱，免官，以王就第。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of his extravagance and indulgence, removed his offices and reduced him to prince living at his estate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor removed his offices for extravagance and reduced him to prince living at his estate.

sentences.zh: 左武衛將軍劉升諫曰：「秦王非有他過，但費官物營廨舍而已。

translations.literal: General of the Left Martial Guard Liu Sheng remonstrated: 'The Prince of Qin has no other fault—he merely spent government goods to build official quarters.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Left Martial Guard Liu Sheng remonstrated: "The Prince of Qin has no other fault—he merely spent government goods to build official quarters.

sentences.zh: 臣謂可容。」

translations.literal: Your subject considers this tolerable.
translations.idiomatic: I consider this tolerable.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「法不可違。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'The law cannot be violated.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The law cannot be violated."

sentences.zh: 升固諫，上忿然作色，升乃止。

translations.literal: Sheng firmly remonstrated. The emperor angrily changed color, and Sheng then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sheng firmly remonstrated; the emperor's expression darkened with anger, and Liu Sheng stopped.

sentences.zh: 其後楊素複進諫曰：「秦王之過，不應至此，願陛下詳之。」

translations.literal: Afterward Yang Su again remonstrated: 'The Prince of Qin's fault should not have reached this point. I wish Your Majesty would examine it carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Su remonstrated again: "The Prince of Qin's fault should not have reached this point—I wish Your Majesty would reconsider.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「我是五兒之父，若如公意，何不別制天子兒律？

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I am the father of five sons. If it were as you suggest, why not separately establish laws for the Son of Heaven's sons?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I am the father of five sons—if it were as you suggest, why not make separate laws for the emperor's sons?

sentences.zh: 以周公之為人，尚誅管、蔡，我誠不及周公遠矣，安能虧法乎？」

translations.literal: Even a man like the Duke of Zhou still executed Guan and Cai. I truly fall far short of the Duke of Zhou—how could I impair the law?'
translations.idiomatic: Even the Duke of Zhou executed Guan and Cai—I fall far short of him; how could I impair the law?"

sentences.zh: 卒不許。

translations.literal: He ultimately did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He ultimately refused.

sentences.zh: 俊疾篤，未能起，遣使奉表陳謝。

translations.literal: Jun's illness was severe and he could not rise. He sent an emissary to submit a memorial expressing repentance.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's illness was severe and he could not rise; he sent an emissary to submit a memorial of repentance.

sentences.zh: 上謂其使曰：「我戮力關塞，創茲大業，作訓垂範，庶臣下守之而不失。

translations.literal: The emperor said to his emissary: 'I exerted myself at the passes and frontiers and created this great enterprise, establishing teachings to serve as models, hoping my subjects would uphold them without loss.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his emissary: "I exerted myself at the frontier and created this great enterprise, establishing teachings as models, hoping my subjects would uphold them.

sentences.zh: 汝為吾子，而欲敗之，不知何以責汝！」

translations.literal: You are my son, yet you wish to ruin it—I do not know how to reproach you!
translations.idiomatic: You are my son, yet you wish to ruin it—I do not know how to reproach you!

sentences.zh: 俊慚怖，疾甚。

translations.literal: Jun was ashamed and fearful, and his illness grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was ashamed and fearful, and his illness grew worse.

sentences.zh: 大都督皇甫統上表，請複王官，不許。

translations.literal: Great Commander Huangfu Tong submitted a memorial requesting restoration of princely offices—it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Great Commander Huangfu Tong submitted a memorial requesting restoration of Jun's princely offices—it was refused.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以疾篤，複拜上柱國。

translations.literal: After more than a year, because his illness was severe, he was again appointed Grand Preceptor of State.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, because his illness was severe, he was again appointed Grand Preceptor of State.

sentences.zh: 二十年六月，薨于秦邸。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twentieth year he died at the Qin residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twentieth year he died at the Qin residence.

sentences.zh: 上哭之數聲而已。

translations.literal: The emperor wept for him only a few cries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept for him only briefly.

sentences.zh: 俊所為侈麗之物，悉命焚之。

translations.literal: All the extravagant and splendid things Jun had made were ordered burned.
translations.idiomatic: All the extravagant things Jun had made were ordered burned.

sentences.zh: 敕送終之具，務從儉約，以為後法也。

translations.literal: Funeral implements were ordered to be strictly simple and economical, to serve as a model for the future.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral arrangements were ordered to be strictly simple, to serve as a model for the future.

sentences.zh: 王府僚佐請立碑，上曰：「欲求名，一卷史書足矣，何用碑為？

translations.literal: The prince's household staff requested a stele. The emperor said: 'If one seeks fame, one volume of historical records is enough—what use is a stele?
translations.idiomatic: The prince's staff requested a stele; the emperor said: "If one seeks fame, one volume of history is enough—what use is a stele?

sentences.zh: 若子孫不能保家，徒與人作鎮石耳。」

translations.literal: If descendants cannot preserve the family, it would merely serve as a gate stone for others."
translations.idiomatic: If descendants cannot preserve the family, it would merely serve as a gate stone for others."

sentences.zh: 妃崔氏以毒王之故，下詔廢絕，賜死於其家。

translations.literal: Consort Lady Cui, because she had poisoned the prince, was by edict deposed and severed, granted death at her home.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Lady Cui, for poisoning the prince, was deposed by edict and ordered to die at her home.

sentences.zh: 子浩，崔氏所生也。

translations.literal: His son Hao was born of Lady Cui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hao was born of Lady Cui.

sentences.zh: 庶子曰湛。

translations.literal: The son by a concubine was Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: The son by a concubine was Zhan.

sentences.zh: 群臣議曰：「《春秋》之義，母以子貴，子以母貴。

translations.literal: The ministers deliberated, saying: 'According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, the mother is ennobled through the son, and the son is ennobled through the mother.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers deliberated: "According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, the mother is ennobled through the son, and the son through the mother.

sentences.zh: 貴既如此，罪則可知。

translations.literal: If ennoblement is thus, guilt is likewise clear.
translations.idiomatic: If ennoblement works thus, guilt works likewise.

sentences.zh: 故漢時栗姬有罪，其子便廢，郭后被廢，其子斯黜。

translations.literal: Therefore in Han times when Lady Li had guilt, her son was deposed; when Empress Guo was deposed, her son Si was removed.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times when Lady Li was guilty, her son was deposed; when Empress Guo was deposed, her son was removed.

sentences.zh: 大既然矣，小亦宜同。

translations.literal: Since the great principle is thus established, the lesser should follow the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Since the great principle is established, the lesser should follow.

sentences.zh: 今秦王二子，母皆罪廢，不合承嗣。」

translations.literal: Now the Prince of Qin's two sons—both their mothers were guilty and deposed—they are not fit to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin's two sons—both their mothers were guilty and deposed—are not fit to inherit.

sentences.zh: 於是以秦國官為喪主。

translations.literal: Thereupon officials of the Qin state were made chief mourners.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Qin state were then made chief mourners.

sentences.zh: 俊長女永豐公主，年十二，遭父憂，哀慕盡禮，免喪，遂絕魚肉。

translations.literal: Jun's eldest daughter, the Princess of Yongfeng, was twelve years old. Encountering her father's bereavement, she mourned with full ritual propriety. After the mourning period ended, she ceased eating fish and meat.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's eldest daughter, the Princess of Yongfeng, was twelve; mourning her father with full propriety, she ceased eating fish and meat after the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 每至忌日，輒流涕不食。

translations.literal: On each anniversary of his death she would weep and not eat.
translations.idiomatic: On each anniversary of his death she wept and would not eat.

sentences.zh: 有開府王延者，性忠厚，領親信兵十餘年，俊甚禮之。

translations.literal: There was an Establishment Commander Wang Yan, by nature loyal and honest, who led trusted troops for more than ten years. Jun greatly honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Establishment Commander Wang Yan, loyal and honest by nature, led trusted troops for more than ten years and was greatly honored by Jun.

sentences.zh: 及俊有疾，延恆在閤下，衣不解帶。

translations.literal: When Jun fell ill, Yan was constantly below the gate, never removing his belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun fell ill, Yan stayed constantly at his door, never removing his belt.

sentences.zh: 俊薨，勺飲不入口者數日，羸頓骨立。

translations.literal: When Jun died, Yan took no spoonful or drink for several days, becoming emaciated until only bones remained.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun died, Yan took no food or drink for several days and became emaciated.

sentences.zh: 上聞而憫之，賜以禦藥，授驃騎將軍，典宿衛。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of this and pitied him, granting him imperial medicine and appointing him General of Agile Cavalry in charge of palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of this and pitied him, granting him imperial medicine and appointing him General of Agile Cavalry in charge of palace guard.

sentences.zh: 俊葬之日，延號慟而絕。

translations.literal: On the day of Jun's burial, Yan wailed and wept until he died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of Jun's burial, Yan wailed until he died.

sentences.zh: 上嗟異之，令通事舍人弔祭焉。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in wonder and ordered a Palace Attendant to offer condolences and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled at this and ordered a Palace Attendant to offer condolences and sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 詔葬延於俊墓側。

translations.literal: By edict Yan was buried beside Jun's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: By edict Yan was buried beside Jun's tomb.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，立浩為秦王，以奉孝王嗣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, he established Hao as Prince of Qin to continue Prince Xiao's line.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, he made Hao Prince of Qin to continue Prince Xiao's line.

sentences.zh: 封湛為濟北侯。

translations.literal: Zhan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 後以浩為河陽都尉。

translations.literal: Later Hao was appointed Commandant of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hao was appointed Commandant of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感作逆之際，左翊衛大將軍宇文述勒兵討之。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, General of the Left Wing Guard Yuwen Shu led troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, General of the Left Wing Guard Yuwen Shu led troops against him.

sentences.zh: 至河陽，修啟於浩，浩複詣述營，兵相往復。

translations.literal: Arriving at Heyang, he sent a letter to Hao; Hao again went to Shu's camp, and troops passed back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Arriving at Heyang, Yuwen Shu sent a letter to Hao; Hao visited Shu's camp in return, and troops passed back and forth.

sentences.zh: 有司劾浩，以諸侯交通內臣，竟坐廢免。

translations.literal: The responsible offices impeached Hao for a feudal lord communicating with inner officials; he was ultimately deposed and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials impeached Hao for a feudal lord communicating with inner officials; he was ultimately deposed.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及殺逆之始，立浩為帝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, he established Hao as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, he made Hao emperor.

sentences.zh: 化及敗于黎陽，北走魏縣，自僭偽號，因而害之。

translations.literal: Huaji was defeated at Liyang, fled north to Wei County, arrogated a false title, and thereby killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji was defeated at Liyang, fled north to Wei County, took a false imperial title, and killed Hao.

sentences.zh: 湛驍果，有膽烈。

translations.literal: Zhan was fierce and resolute, with bold courage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was fierce and resolute, with bold courage.

sentences.zh: 大業初，為滎陽太守，坐浩免，亦為化及所害。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he served as Governor of Xingyang; implicated by Hao's fall, he was also killed by Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye he served as Governor of Xingyang; implicated by Hao's fall, he was also killed by Huaji.

sentences.zh: 庶人秀庶人秀，高祖第四子也，

translations.literal: Commoner Xiu, Yang Xiu, was the fourth son of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu, later the commoner Xiu, was the fourth son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 立為越王。

translations.literal: He was established as Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徙封於蜀，拜柱國、益州刺史、總管，二十四州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred and enfeoffed in Shu, appointed Preceptor of State, Governor of Yizhou, and Governor-General over twenty-four prefectures and all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Shu, appointed Preceptor of State, Governor of Yizhou, and Governor-General over twenty-four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二年，進位上柱國、西南道行台尚書令，本官如故。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to Grand Preceptor of State and Director of the Southwest Circuit Executive and Minister of State Affairs, his original offices remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to Grand Preceptor of State and Director of the Southwest Circuit Executive, retaining his other offices.

sentences.zh: 歲餘而罷。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十二年，又為內史令、右領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he again served as Director of the Inner Scribe and General of the Right Forward Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he again served as Director of the Inner Scribe and General of the Right Forward Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋複出鎮於蜀。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was again sent out to garrison Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was again posted to garrison Shu.

sentences.zh: 秀有膽氣，容貌瑰偉，美須髯，多武藝，甚為朝臣所憚。

translations.literal: Xiu had bold spirit; his appearance was magnificent, his beard and whiskers handsome, and he was skilled in many martial arts—court ministers greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was bold in spirit, magnificent in appearance, with a handsome beard; skilled in many martial arts, he was greatly feared by court ministers.

sentences.zh: 上每謂獻皇后曰：「秀必以惡終。

translations.literal: The emperor often said to Empress Xian: 'Xiu will surely meet an evil end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often told Empress Dugu: "Xiu will surely meet an evil end.

sentences.zh: 我在當無慮，至兄弟必反。」

translations.literal: While I am alive there should be no worry, but when it comes to his brothers he will surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: While I live there is no worry, but toward his brothers he will surely rebel.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎元衡使於蜀，秀深結於衡，以左右為請。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Ministry of War Yuan Heng was sent on mission to Shu. Xiu formed deep ties with Heng and requested additional attendants through him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Ministry of War Yuan Heng was sent on mission to Shu; Xiu formed deep ties with him and requested additional attendants.

sentences.zh: 既還京師，請益左右，上不許。

translations.literal: After returning to the capital, he requested more attendants—the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital, Xiu requested more attendants—the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 大將軍劉噲之討西爨也，高祖令上開府楊武通將兵繼進。

translations.literal: When General Liu Huai attacked the Western Cuan, Gaozu ordered Establishment General Yang Wutong to lead troops in follow-up advance.
translations.idiomatic: When General Liu Huai attacked the Western Cuan, Emperor Wen ordered Establishment General Yang Wutong to lead troops in support.

sentences.zh: 秀使嬖人萬智光為武通行軍司馬，上以秀任非其人，譴責之。

translations.literal: Xiu had his favorite Wan Zhiguang serve as Yang Wutong's campaign major. The emperor, because Xiu had appointed an unworthy person, reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu appointed his favorite Wan Zhiguang as Yang Wutong's campaign major; the emperor reproached him for appointing an unworthy person.

sentences.zh: 因謂群臣曰：「壞我法者，必在子孫乎？

translations.literal: He thereupon said to the ministers: 'Those who ruin my laws—must they be among my descendants?
translations.idiomatic: He told the ministers: "Must those who ruin my laws be among my own descendants?

sentences.zh: 譬如猛獸，物不能害，反為毛間蟲所損食耳。」

translations.literal: It is like a fierce beast that nothing can harm, yet is damaged and eaten by insects in its fur.
translations.idiomatic: It is like a fierce beast that nothing can harm, yet is eaten by insects in its fur.

sentences.zh: 於是遂分秀所統。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiu's jurisdiction was divided.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's jurisdiction was then divided.

sentences.zh: 秀漸奢侈，違犯制度，車馬被服，擬于天子。

translations.literal: Xiu gradually became extravagant, violated regulations, and his carriages, horses, and garments rivaled the Son of Heaven's.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu gradually grew extravagant, violated regulations, and his carriages, horses, and garments rivaled the emperor's.

sentences.zh: 及太子勇以讒毀廢，晉王廣為皇太子，秀意甚不平。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Yong was deposed through slander and the Prince of Jin, Guang, became crown prince, Xiu was greatly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Yong was deposed through slander and the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, became crown prince, Xiu was greatly resentful.

sentences.zh: 皇太子恐秀終為後變，陰令楊素求其罪而譖之，

translations.literal: The crown prince feared Xiu would ultimately cause future trouble and secretly ordered Yang Su to seek his crimes and slander him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince feared Xiu would cause future trouble and secretly ordered Yang Su to find fault with him and slander him.

sentences.zh: 仁壽二年，征還京師，上見，不與語。

translations.literal: In the second year of Renshou, he was summoned back to the capital. When the emperor saw him, he did not speak to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Renshou, Xiu was summoned back to the capital; when the emperor saw him, he did not speak to him.

sentences.zh: 明日，使使切讓之。

translations.literal: The next day he sent emissaries to sternly reproach him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent envoys to sternly reproach him.

sentences.zh: 秀謝曰：「忝荷國恩，出臨籓嶽，不能奉法，罪當萬死。」

translations.literal: Xiu apologized, saying: 'I am unworthy of the state's grace in going out to govern a frontier province; I could not uphold the law—my crime deserves ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu apologized: "I am unworthy of the state's grace in governing a frontier province; I failed to uphold the law—my crime deserves death.

sentences.zh: 皇太子及諸王流涕庭謝。

translations.literal: The crown prince and the princes wept in the courtyard pleading for mercy.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and the other princes wept in the courtyard pleading for mercy.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「頃者秦王糜費財物，我以父道訓之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Recently the Prince of Qin wasted goods and wealth—I admonished him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Recently the Prince of Qin wasted goods—I admonished him as a father.

sentences.zh: 今秀蠹害生民，當以君道繩之。」

translations.literal: Now Xiu harms and injures the people—he should be restrained by the ruler's way.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xiu harms the people—he must be restrained as a ruler would.

sentences.zh: 於是付執法者。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was handed over to the law officers.
translations.idiomatic: He was then handed over to the law officers.

sentences.zh: 開府慶整諫曰：「庶人勇既廢，秦王已薨，陛下兒子無多，何至如是？

translations.literal: Establishment General Qing Zheng remonstrated: 'Commoner Yong is already deposed and the Prince of Qin has died—Your Majesty has not many sons; why go this far?
translations.idiomatic: Establishment General Qing Zheng remonstrated: "Commoner Yong is deposed and the Prince of Qin is dead—Your Majesty has few sons; why go this far?

sentences.zh: 然蜀王性甚耿介，今被重責，恐不自全。」

translations.literal: Yet the Prince of Shu's nature is very upright and unyielding; now that he bears heavy blame, I fear he may not preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Prince of Shu is very upright by nature; under such heavy blame, I fear he may not survive.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，欲斷其舌。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and wished to cut out his tongue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and wished to cut out his tongue.

sentences.zh: 因謂群臣曰：「當斬秀於市，以謝百姓。」

translations.literal: He thereupon said to the ministers: 'Xiu should be beheaded in the marketplace to appease the people.
translations.idiomatic: He told the ministers: "Xiu should be beheaded in the marketplace to appease the people.

sentences.zh: 乃令楊素、蘇威、牛弘、柳述、趙綽等推治之。

translations.literal: He then ordered Yang Su, Su Wei, Niu Hong, Liu Shu, Zhao Chuo, and others to investigate and try the case.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yang Su, Su Wei, Niu Hong, Liu Shu, Zhao Chuo, and others to investigate the case.

sentences.zh: 太子陰作偶人，書上及漢王姓字，縛手釘心，令人埋之華山下，令楊素髮之。

translations.literal: The crown prince secretly made effigies, wrote the emperor's and the Prince of Han's names on them, bound their hands and nailed their hearts, had people bury them beneath Mount Hua, and ordered Yang Su to dig them up.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince secretly made effigies bearing the emperor's and the Prince of Han's names, bound their hands and nailed their hearts, had them buried beneath Mount Hua, and ordered Yang Su to dig them up.

sentences.zh: 又作檄文曰：「逆臣賊子，專弄威柄，陛下唯守虛器，一無所知。」

translations.literal: He also composed a proclamation saying: 'Rebellious ministers and wicked sons monopolize power; Your Majesty merely holds an empty vessel and knows nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: He also forged a proclamation: "Rebellious ministers and wicked sons monopolize power; Your Majesty merely holds an empty vessel and knows nothing.

sentences.zh: 陳甲兵之盛，雲「指期問罪」。

translations.literal: He described the abundance of armored troops, saying 'a set date to demand punishment.'
translations.idiomatic: It described abundant armored troops and declared "a set date to demand punishment."

sentences.zh: 置秀集中，因以聞奏。

translations.literal: These were placed among Xiu's possessions and thereby reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: These were planted among Xiu's possessions and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「天下寧有是耶！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Can such a thing exist under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Can such a thing exist under Heaven!

sentences.zh: 於是廢為庶人，幽內侍省，不得與妻子相見，令給獠婢二人驅使。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was deposed to commoner status, confined in the Inner Attendant Directorate, not permitted to see his wife and children, and given two Liao maidservants for service.
translations.idiomatic: He was deposed to commoner status, confined in the Inner Attendant Directorate, forbidden to see his wife and children, and given two Liao maidservants.

sentences.zh: 與相連坐者百餘人。

translations.literal: More than a hundred people were implicated by association.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred people were implicated.

sentences.zh: 秀既幽逼，憤懣不知所為，乃上表曰：「臣以多幸，聯慶皇枝，蒙天慈鞠養，九歲榮貴，唯知富樂，未嘗憂懼。

translations.literal: Xiu, now confined and pressed, was resentful and did not know what to do. He submitted a memorial, saying: 'Your subject, through much fortune, joined in celebrating the imperial branch, received Heaven's compassionate nurturing, and at nine years enjoyed honor and wealth—knowing only riches and pleasure, never anxiety or fear.
translations.idiomatic: Confined and desperate, Xiu submitted a memorial: "Through great fortune I joined the imperial branch, was nurtured by Heaven's compassion, and at nine enjoyed honor and wealth—knowing only riches and pleasure, never fear.

sentences.zh: 輕恣愚心，陷茲刑網，負深山嶽，甘心九泉。

translations.literal: Lightly indulging my foolish heart, I fell into this net of punishment; bearing mountains of guilt, I am willing to descend to the nine springs.
translations.idiomatic: Indulging my foolish heart, I fell into this punishment; bearing guilt as heavy as mountains, I am willing to die.

sentences.zh: 不謂天恩尚假餘漏，至如今者，方知愚心不可縱，國法不可犯，撫膺念咎，自新莫及。

translations.literal: I did not expect Heaven's grace still to grant me remaining breath. Only now do I know the foolish heart cannot be indulged and state law cannot be violated. Beating my breast and reflecting on my fault, reform comes too late.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect Heaven's grace to spare me; only now do I know the foolish heart cannot be indulged and state law cannot be violated—beating my breast, I see reform comes too late.

sentences.zh: 猶望分身竭命，少答慈造，但以靈祗不祜，福祿消盡，夫婦抱思，不相勝致。

translations.literal: I still hope to give my body and exhaust my life to slightly repay compassionate creation, but spirits and gods do not bless me; fortune and emolument are exhausted; husband and wife hold longing they cannot bear to express.
translations.idiomatic: I still hope to give my life to repay your compassion, but fortune is exhausted and my wife and I hold longing we cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 只恐長辭明世，永歸泉壤，伏願慈恩，賜垂矜湣，殘息未盡之間，希與爪子相見。

translations.literal: I only fear long parting from the bright world and eternal return to the dark earth. Prostrate, I wish compassionate grace and beg pity; while my remaining breath is not yet exhausted, I hope to see my Zhua-zi once more.
translations.idiomatic: I fear eternal parting from this world; I beg compassionate grace—while my breath remains, I hope to see my beloved son once more.

sentences.zh: 請賜一穴，令骸骨有所。」

translations.literal: I request a grave be granted so my bones may have a resting place.
translations.idiomatic: I request a grave so my bones may have a resting place.

sentences.zh: 爪子即其愛子也。

translations.literal: Zhua-zi was his beloved son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhua-zi was his beloved son.

sentences.zh: 上因下詔數其罪曰：

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon issued an edict enumerating his crimes, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict enumerating his crimes:

sentences.zh: 汝地居臣子，情兼家國，庸、蜀要重，委以鎮之。

translations.literal: You by position are a subject, yet in feeling you share in family and state. Yong and Shu are strategically vital—I entrusted you to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: You are a subject who shares in family and state; Yong and Shu are strategically vital—I entrusted you to garrison them.

sentences.zh: 汝乃干紀亂常，懷惡樂禍，䁹睨二宮，佇遲災釁，容納不逞，結構異端。

translations.literal: Yet you violated discipline and disrupted norms, harbored evil and delighted in calamity, cast covetous eyes on the two palaces, awaited disaster and strife, harbored the unrestrained, and formed heterodox factions.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you violated discipline, harbored evil and delighted in calamity, cast covetous eyes on the two palaces, awaited disaster, harbored the unrestrained, and formed heterodox factions.

sentences.zh: 我有不和，汝便覘候，望我不起，便有異心。

translations.literal: When I was unwell, you watched and waited; hoping I would not rise, you harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: When I was unwell, you watched and waited; hoping I would not recover, you harbored rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 皇太子汝兄也，次當建立，汝假託妖言，乃雲不終其位。

translations.literal: The crown prince is your elder brother and next in line for establishment—yet you falsely invoked demonic words, saying he would not complete his tenure.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is your elder brother and heir—you falsely invoked omens, saying he would not complete his tenure.

sentences.zh: 妄稱鬼怪，又道不得入宮，自言骨相非人臣，德業堪承重器，妄道清城出聖，欲以己當之，詐稱益州龍見，托言吉兆。

translations.literal: You groundlessly spoke of ghosts and monsters, also saying you could not enter the palace, claiming your bone structure was not that of a subject, that your virtue and achievements could bear the great vessel, groundlessly saying a sage would emerge from Qingcheng and wishing to take that place yourself, falsely claiming a dragon appeared in Yizhou as an auspicious omen.
translations.idiomatic: You spoke groundlessly of ghosts, claimed you could not enter the palace, said your bone structure was not that of a subject and your virtue could bear the great vessel, claimed a sage would emerge from Qingcheng and wished to take that place, and falsely claimed a dragon appeared in Yizhou as an omen.

sentences.zh: 重述木易之姓，更治成都之宮；

translations.literal: You repeatedly spoke of the surname Mu-Yi and rebuilt the palace at Chengdu;
translations.idiomatic: You repeatedly spoke of the surname Mu-Yi and rebuilt the palace at Chengdu;

sentences.zh: 妄說禾乃之名，以當八千之運。

translations.literal: groundlessly spoke the name He-Nai to correspond to the fortune of eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: groundlessly spoke the name He-Nai to claim the fortune of eight thousand years.

sentences.zh: 橫生京師妖異，以證父兄之災；

translations.literal: You groundlessly produced strange omens in the capital to prove disaster for father and brothers;
translations.idiomatic: You groundlessly produced strange omens in the capital to prove disaster for father and brothers;

sentences.zh: 妄造蜀地徵祥，以符己身之籙。

translations.literal: groundlessly fabricated auspicious signs in Shu to match your own destiny.
translations.idiomatic: and groundlessly fabricated auspicious signs in Shu to match your own destiny.

sentences.zh: 汝豈不欲得國家惡也，天下亂也，輒造白玉之珽，又為白羽之箭，文物服飾，豈似有君，鳩集左道，符書厭鎮。

translations.literal: Did you not wish the state ill and the realm in chaos? You made white jade scepters and white-feathered arrows; your cultural objects and garments—did they not resemble those of a ruler? You gathered heterodox ways, talisman writings, and apotropaic charms.
translations.idiomatic: Did you not wish the state ill and the realm in chaos? You made white jade scepters and white-feathered arrows; your regalia resembled a ruler's; you gathered heterodox ways, talismans, and apotropaic charms.

sentences.zh: 漢王於汝，親則弟也，乃畫其形像，書其姓名，縛手釘心，枷鎖杻械。

translations.literal: The Prince of Han to you is close as a younger brother—yet you painted his image, wrote his name, bound his hands and nailed his heart, and put him in cangue, chains, and shackles.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Han is your younger brother—yet you painted his image, wrote his name, bound his hands and nailed his heart, and put him in chains and shackles.

sentences.zh: 仍雲請西嶽華山慈父聖母神兵九億萬騎，收楊諒魂神，閉在華山下，勿令散蕩。

translations.literal: You also said you invoked the compassionate father and holy mother of Mount Hua of the Western Peak, with nine hundred million divine troops, to seize Yang Liang's soul and confine it beneath Mount Hua, not letting it wander.
translations.idiomatic: You also claimed to invoke the divine troops of Mount Hua to seize Yang Liang's soul and confine it beneath the mountain.

sentences.zh: 我之於汝，親則父也，複雲請西嶽華山慈父呈母，賜為開化楊堅夫妻，回心歡喜。

translations.literal: I to you am close as a father—yet you also said you invoked the compassionate father and holy mother of Mount Hua of the Western Peak, granting them as the couple Yang Jian of Kaihua, who turned their hearts in joy.
translations.idiomatic: I am your father—yet you also claimed to invoke the divine parents of Mount Hua as the couple Yang Jian of Kaihua, rejoicing in their favor.

sentences.zh: 又畫我形像，縛手撮頭，仍雲請西嶽神兵收楊堅魂神。

translations.literal: You also painted my image, bound the hands and grasped the head, and still said you invoked the divine troops of the Western Peak to seize Yang Jian's soul.
translations.idiomatic: You also painted my image with bound hands and grasped head, claiming to invoke Mount Hua's divine troops to seize Yang Jian's soul.

sentences.zh: 如此形狀，我今不知楊諒、楊堅是汝何親也？

translations.literal: In such form—what kin are Yang Liang and Yang Jian to you?
translations.idiomatic: In such form—what kin are Yang Liang and Yang Jian to you?

sentences.zh: 苞藏凶慝，圖謀不軌，逆臣之跡也；

translations.literal: Harboring fierce wickedness and plotting unlawful designs—the marks of a rebellious subject;
translations.idiomatic: Harboring fierce wickedness and plotting unlawful designs—the mark of a rebellious subject;

sentences.zh: 希父之災，以為身幸，賊子之心也；

translations.literal: Hoping for your father's disaster as your own fortune—the heart of a wicked son;
translations.idiomatic: Hoping for your father's disaster as your own fortune—the heart of a wicked son;

sentences.zh: 懷非分之望，肆毒心于兄，悖弟之行也；

translations.literal: Harborin improper ambitions and unleashing poisonous intent upon your elder brother—the conduct of a rebellious younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Harboring improper ambitions and unleashing malice upon your elder brother—the conduct of a rebellious younger brother;

sentences.zh: 嫉妒于弟，無惡不為，無孔懷之情也；

translations.literal: Jealous of your younger brother, doing every evil—no brotherly feeling from the same womb;
translations.idiomatic: Jealous of your younger brother, doing every evil—no brotherly feeling;

sentences.zh: 違犯制度，壞亂之極也；

translations.literal: Violating regulations—the height of ruin and disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Violating regulations—the height of disorder;

sentences.zh: 多殺不幸，豺狼之暴也；

translations.literal: Killing many innocents—the cruelty of wolves;
translations.idiomatic: Killing many innocents—the cruelty of wolves;

sentences.zh: 剝削民庶，酷虐之甚也；

translations.literal: Exploiting the common people—the extremity of cruel tyranny;
translations.idiomatic: Exploiting the common people—the extremity of cruel tyranny;

sentences.zh: 唯求財貨，市井之業也；

translations.literal: Seeking only wealth and goods—the trade of the marketplace;
translations.idiomatic: Seeking only wealth—the trade of the marketplace;

sentences.zh: 專事妖邪，頑囂之性也；

translations.literal: Devoting yourself to demonic evil—the nature of the stubborn and arrogant;
translations.idiomatic: Devoting yourself to demonic evil—the nature of the stubborn and arrogant;

sentences.zh: 弗克負荷，不材之器也。

translations.literal: Unable to bear the burden—a vessel of no talent.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bear the burden—a vessel of no talent.

sentences.zh: 凡此十者，滅天理，逆人倫，汝皆為之，不祥之甚也，欲免禍患，長守富貴，其可得乎！

translations.literal: All these ten—destroying Heaven's principle and violating human relations—you have done them all; how extremely inauspicious! To wish to escape calamity and long preserve wealth and honor—can that be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: All ten of these—destroying Heaven's principle and violating human relations—you have done them all; how inauspicious! To wish to escape calamity and preserve wealth and honor—can that be obtained?

sentences.zh: 後複聽與其子同處。

translations.literal: Later he was again permitted to live together with his son.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again permitted to live with his son.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，禁錮如初。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, confinement continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, confinement continued as before.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之弑逆也，欲立秀為帝，群議不許。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, he wished to establish Xiu as emperor—the assembled opinion did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, he wished to make Xiu emperor—the assembled opinion did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 於是害之，並其諸子。

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed him, together with all his sons.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed Xiu, together with all his sons.

sentences.zh: 庶人諒，字德章，一名傑，，立為漢王。

translations.literal: Commoner Liang, Yang Liang, courtesy name Dezhang, also named Jie, was established as Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Liang, later the commoner Liang, whose courtesy name was Dezhang and who was also named Jie, was made Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 十二年，為雍州牧，加上柱國、右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he served as Governor of Yongzhou, additionally appointed Grand Preceptor of State and General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he served as Governor of Yongzhou and was additionally appointed Grand Preceptor of State and General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was transferred to General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 十七年，出為并州總管，上幸溫湯而送之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was sent out as Governor-General of Bingzhou; the emperor visited the hot springs to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was posted as Governor-General of Bingzhou; the emperor visited the hot springs to see him off.

sentences.zh: 自山以東，至於滄海，南拒黃河，五十二州盡隸焉。

translations.literal: From east of the mountains to the sea, south to the Yellow River—all fifty-two prefectures were placed under his authority.
translations.idiomatic: From east of the mountains to the sea, south to the Yellow River—all fifty-two prefectures were under his authority.

sentences.zh: 特許以便宜，不拘律令。

translations.literal: He was specially permitted discretionary authority, not bound by statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially granted discretionary authority, not bound by statutes.

sentences.zh: 十八年，起遼東之役，以諒為行軍元帥，率眾至遼水，遇疾疫，不利而還。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Liaodong campaign was launched; Liang served as campaign commander, leading troops to the Liao River; encountering epidemic disease, they fared poorly and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the Liaodong campaign was launched; Liang served as campaign commander, leading troops to the Liao River; epidemic disease forced a retreat.

sentences.zh: 十九年，突厥犯塞，以諒為行軍元帥，竟不臨戎。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year when the Turks violated the frontier, Liang served as campaign commander but ultimately did not go to battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year when the Turks raided the frontier, Liang served as campaign commander but never went to battle.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚寵愛之。

translations.literal: Gaozu greatly favored and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen greatly favored him.

sentences.zh: 諒自以所居天下精兵處，以太子讒廢，居常怏怏，陰有異圖。

translations.literal: Liang, considering that his post was where the realm's elite troops were stationed and that the crown prince had been deposed through slander, was constantly resentful and secretly harbored rebellious designs.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, holding the realm's elite troops and seeing the crown prince deposed through slander, was constantly resentful and secretly harbored rebellious designs.

sentences.zh: 遂諷高祖雲：「突厥方強，太原即為重鎮，宜修武備。」

translations.literal: He thereupon remonstrated with Gaozu, saying: 'The Turks are growing strong; Taiyuan is a strategic fortress and military preparations should be strengthened.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated with Emperor Wen: "The Turks are growing strong; Taiyuan is a strategic fortress and military preparations should be strengthened.

sentences.zh: 高祖從之。

translations.literal: Gaozu followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是大發工役，繕治器械，貯納於并州。

translations.literal: Thereupon corvée labor was greatly mobilized, weapons were repaired and prepared, and stores were accumulated at Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée labor was greatly mobilized, weapons were prepared, and stores accumulated at Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 招傭亡命，左右私人，殆將數萬。

translations.literal: Desperate men were recruited and personal retainers gathered—nearly tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Desperate men were recruited and personal retainers gathered—nearly tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 王頍者，梁將王僧辯之子也，少倜儻，有奇略，為諒諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Wang E was the son of the Liang general Wang Sengbian—unconventional in youth, with extraordinary stratagems, he served as Liang's advisory aide.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E, son of the Liang general Wang Sengbian, was unconventional in youth and possessed extraordinary stratagems; he served as Liang's advisory aide.

sentences.zh: 蕭摩訶者，陳氏舊將。

translations.literal: Xiao Mohe was a former general of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Mohe was a former general of Chen.

sentences.zh: 二人俱不得志，每鬱鬱思亂，並為諒所親善。

translations.literal: Both men were frustrated in their ambitions and constantly brooded on rebellion; both were favored and befriended by Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Both were frustrated in their ambitions and constantly brooded on rebellion; both were favored by Liang.

sentences.zh: 及蜀王以罪廢，諒愈不自安。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Shu was deposed for his crimes, Liang grew all the more unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Shu was deposed, Liang grew all the more unsettled.

sentences.zh: 會高祖崩，征之不赴，遂發兵反。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, Liang was summoned but did not come; he thereupon raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen died, Liang was summoned but did not come and raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 總管司馬皇甫誕切諫，諒怒，收擊之。

translations.literal: The governor-general's major Huangfu Dan remonstrated forcefully; Liang was angry and had him arrested and beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General's major Huangfu Dan remonstrated forcefully; Liang had him arrested and beaten.

sentences.zh: 王頍說諒曰：「王所部將吏家屬，盡在關西，若用此等，即宜長驅深入，直據京都，所謂疾雷不及掩耳。

translations.literal: Wang E said to Liang: 'Your officers' and officials' families are all in the Guanxi region. If you use such men, you should drive deep at once and seize the capital directly—as they say, swift thunder gives no time to cover the ears.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E told Liang: "Your officers' families are all in the west; if you use such men, drive deep at once and seize the capital—as they say, swift thunder gives no time to cover the ears.

sentences.zh: 若但欲割據舊齊之地，宜任東人。」

translations.literal: If you only wish to carve out and hold the former territory of Qi, you should employ eastern men.
translations.idiomatic: If you only wish to hold the former Qi territories, employ eastern men.

sentences.zh: 諒不能專定，乃兼用二策，唱言曰：「楊素反，將誅之。」

translations.literal: Liang could not decide exclusively and therefore used both strategies together, proclaiming: 'Yang Su has rebelled—I will execute him.'
translations.idiomatic: Liang could not decide and used both strategies, proclaiming: "Yang Su has rebelled—I will execute him."

sentences.zh: 聞喜人總管府兵曹裴文安說諒曰：「井陘以西，是王掌握之內，山東士馬，亦為我有，宜悉發之。

translations.literal: Pei Wen'an, military clerk of the Wenxi Governor-General's office, said to Liang: 'West of Jingxing Pass is within your grasp; the soldiers and horses of Shandong are also ours—you should mobilize them all.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Wen'an, military clerk of the Wenxi Governor-General's office, told Liang: "West of Jingxing Pass is within your grasp; Shandong's troops are also yours—mobilize them all.

sentences.zh: 分遣羸兵，屯守要路，仍令隨方略地。

translations.literal: Dispatch weak troops to garrison strategic routes, and still order them to seize territory as they advance.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch weak troops to garrison strategic routes and seize territory as they advance.

sentences.zh: 率其精銳，直入蒲津。

translations.literal: Lead the elite forces straight into Pujin.
translations.idiomatic: Lead the elite forces straight to Pujin.

sentences.zh: 文安請為前鋒，王以大軍繼後，風行電擊，頓於霸上，咸陽以東可指麾而定。

translations.literal: Wen'an requested to serve as vanguard; the prince would follow with the main army—moving like wind and striking like lightning, halting at Bashang, and east of Xianyang could be secured at a gesture.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an offered to serve as vanguard while Liang followed with the main army—moving like wind and striking like lightning, halting at Bashang; east of Xianyang could be secured at a gesture.

sentences.zh: 京師震擾，兵不暇集，上下相疑，群情離駭，我即陳兵號令，誰敢不從，旬日之間，事可定矣。」

translations.literal: The capital would be shaken and disturbed; troops would have no time to assemble; superiors and inferiors would suspect each other; the multitude would scatter in alarm. We would then deploy troops and issue commands—who would dare not obey? Within ten days the matter could be settled.'
translations.idiomatic: The capital would be shaken; troops would have no time to assemble; superiors and inferiors would suspect each other; the people would scatter in alarm. Deploy troops and issue commands—who would dare disobey? Within ten days the matter could be settled."

sentences.zh: 諒大悅。

translations.literal: Liang was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 於是遣所署大將軍余公理出太谷，以趣河陽。

translations.literal: He thereupon dispatched his appointed Grand General Yu Gongli out through Taigu toward Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched his appointed Grand General Yu Gongli through Taigu toward Heyang.

sentences.zh: 大將軍綦良出滏口，以趣黎陽。

translations.literal: Grand General Qi Liang went out through Fukou toward Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Qi Liang went out through Fukou toward Liyang.

sentences.zh: 大將軍劉建出井陘，以略燕趙。

translations.literal: Grand General Liu Jian went out through Jingxing to overrun Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Liu Jian went out through Jingxing to overrun Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 柱國喬鐘葵出雁門。

translations.literal: Preceptor of State Qiao Zhongkui went out through Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Preceptor of State Qiao Zhongkui went out through Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 署文安為柱國，紇單貴、王聃、大將軍茹茹天保、侯莫陳惠直指京師。

translations.literal: Wen'an was appointed Preceptor of State; Gedan Gui, Wang Dan, Grand General Ruru Tianbao, and Houmochen Hui marched directly on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an was appointed Preceptor of State; Gedan Gui, Wang Dan, Grand General Ruru Tianbao, and Houmochen Hui marched directly on the capital.

sentences.zh: 未至蒲津百餘里，諒忽改圖，令紇單貴斷河橋，守蒲州，而召文安。

translations.literal: When they were still more than a hundred li from Pujin, Liang suddenly changed his plan, ordering Gedan Gui to destroy the river bridge, hold Puzhou, and summoning Wen'an back.
translations.idiomatic: When still more than a hundred li from Pujin, Liang suddenly changed his plan, ordering Gedan Gui to destroy the river bridge, hold Puzhou, and summoning Wen'an back.

sentences.zh: 文安至曰：「兵機詭速，本欲出其不意。

translations.literal: When Wen'an arrived he said: 'Military opportunity is cunning and swift—we intended to catch them unawares.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen'an arrived he said: "Military opportunity is cunning and swift—we intended to catch them unawares.

sentences.zh: 王既不行，文安又退，使彼計成，大事去矣。」

translations.literal: The prince would not advance and Wen'an has retreated—letting their plans succeed; the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: You would not advance and I have retreated—letting their plans succeed; the great affair is lost.

sentences.zh: 諒不對。

translations.literal: Liang did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Liang did not reply.

sentences.zh: 以王聃為蒲州刺史，裴文安為晉州，薛粹為絳州，梁菩薩為潞州，韋道正為韓州，張伯英為澤州。

translations.literal: Wang Dan was made Governor of Puzhou; Pei Wen'an of Jinzhou; Xue Cui of Jiangzhou; Liang Pusa of Luzhou; Wei Daozheng of Hanzhou; Zhang Boying of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan was made Governor of Puzhou; Pei Wen'an of Jinzhou; Xue Cui of Jiangzhou; Liang Pusa of Luzhou; Wei Daozheng of Hanzhou; Zhang Boying of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣楊素率騎五千，襲王聃、紇單貴于蒲州，破之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang dispatched Yang Su with five thousand cavalry to strike Wang Dan and Gedan Gui at Puzhou and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang dispatched Yang Su with five thousand cavalry to strike Wang Dan and Gedan Gui at Puzhou and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 於是率步騎四萬趣太原。

translations.literal: He thereupon led forty thousand infantry and cavalry toward Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then led forty thousand infantry and cavalry toward Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 諒使趙子開守高壁，楊素擊走之。

translations.literal: Liang had Zhao Zikai defend Gaobi; Yang Su attacked and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had Zhao Zikai defend Gaobi; Yang Su attacked and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 諒大懼，拒素於蒿澤。

translations.literal: Liang was greatly afraid and blocked Yang Su at Haozhe.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was greatly afraid and blocked Yang Su at Haozhe.

sentences.zh: 屬天大雨，諒欲旋師，王頍諫曰：「楊素懸軍，士馬疲弊，王以銳卒親戎擊之，其勢必舉。

translations.literal: As heavy rain fell, Liang wished to withdraw his army. Wang E remonstrated: 'Yang Su's army is isolated and his men and horses exhausted. If the prince personally leads elite troops to attack, victory is certain.
translations.idiomatic: As heavy rain fell, Liang wished to withdraw. Wang E remonstrated: "Yang Su's army is isolated and exhausted—if you personally lead elite troops to attack, victory is certain.

sentences.zh: 今見敵而還，示人以怯，阻戰士之心，益西軍之氣，願王必勿還也。」

translations.literal: Now to see the enemy and retreat shows cowardice to others, dampens the warriors' hearts, and boosts the western army's morale. I wish the prince absolutely not to retreat.
translations.idiomatic: To see the enemy and retreat shows cowardice, dampens your warriors' hearts, and boosts the enemy's morale—I beg you not to retreat.

sentences.zh: 諒不從，退守清源。

translations.literal: Liang did not follow this advice and withdrew to defend Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang did not listen and withdrew to defend Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 素進擊之，諒勒兵與官軍大戰，死者萬八千人。

translations.literal: Su advanced to attack. Liang marshaled his troops and fought a great battle with the government army; eighteen thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su advanced to attack; Liang marshaled his troops and fought a great battle with the government army—eighteen thousand died.

sentences.zh: 諒退保并州，楊素進兵圍之。

translations.literal: Liang retreated to hold Bingzhou; Yang Su advanced and besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Liang retreated to Bingzhou; Yang Su advanced and besieged it.

sentences.zh: 諒窮蹙，降於素。

translations.literal: Liang, cornered and pressed, surrendered to Su.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Liang surrendered to Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 百僚奏諒罪當死，帝曰：「終鮮兄弟，情不忍言，欲屈法恕諒一死。」

translations.literal: The hundred officials memorialized that Liang's crime deserved death. The emperor said: 'It is rare to have brothers to the end—I cannot bear to speak of it in feeling. I wish to bend the law and spare Liang's life.
translations.idiomatic: Officials memorialized that Liang's crime deserved death. The emperor said: "Brothers are rare to the end—I cannot bear to speak of it; I wish to bend the law and spare Liang's life.

sentences.zh: 於是除名為民，絕其屬籍，竟以幽死。

translations.literal: Thereupon his name was removed and he was made a commoner; his clan register was severed, and he ultimately died in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: His name was removed and he was made a commoner; his clan register was severed, and he ultimately died in confinement.

sentences.zh: 子顥，因而禁錮，宇文化及弑逆之際，遇害。

translations.literal: His son Hao was thereby confined; at the time of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hao was confined and killed during Yuwen Huaji's regicide.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：高祖之子五人，莫有終其天命，異哉！

translations.literal: [Commentary] The historian says: Of Gaozu's five sons, not one completed his allotted span—how strange!
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] The historian says: Of Emperor Wen's five sons, not one completed his allotted span—how strange!

sentences.zh: 房陵資於骨肉之親，篤以君臣之義，經綸締構，契闊夷險，撫軍監國，凡二十年，雖三善未稱，而視膳無闕。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fangling was endowed with flesh-and-blood kinship and steeped in the righteousness of ruler and subject. In planning and founding, through shared hardship and peril, overseeing the army and supervising the state—for twenty years in all—though the three virtues were not fully achieved, his attendance at meals was never lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fangling possessed flesh-and-blood kinship and the righteousness of ruler and subject; in founding the state through hardship, overseeing the army and supervising government for twenty years—though the three virtues were not fully achieved, he never failed in his duties.

sentences.zh: 恩寵既變，讒言間之，顧複之慈，頓隔於人理，父子之道，遂滅於天性。

translations.literal: Once favor and grace changed and slander intervened, the compassion of looking back and turning was suddenly cut off from human principle, and the way of father and son was extinguished in natural affection.
translations.idiomatic: Once favor changed and slander intervened, paternal compassion was cut off from human principle, and the bond of father and son was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 隋室將亡之效，眾庶皆知之矣。

translations.literal: The sign that the Sui house would perish—the common people all knew it.
translations.idiomatic: The sign that the Sui dynasty would perish was known to all.

sentences.zh: 《慎子》有言曰：「一兔走街，百人逐之，積兔於市，過者不顧。」

translations.literal: Master Shen has a saying: 'One rabbit runs through the street and a hundred people chase it; pile rabbits in the market and passersby do not glance at them.
translations.idiomatic: Master Shen said: "One rabbit runs through the street and a hundred people chase it; pile rabbits in the market and passersby do not glance at them.

sentences.zh: 豈有無欲哉？

translations.literal: Is it that they have no desire?
translations.idiomatic: Is it that they have no desire?"

sentences.zh: 分定故也。

translations.literal: It is because shares are fixed.
translations.idiomatic: It is because shares are fixed.

sentences.zh: 房陵分定久矣，高祖一朝易之，開逆亂之源，長覬覦之望。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fangling's share had long been fixed; Gaozu changed it in a single morning, opening the source of rebellion and lengthening the hope of covetous gazes.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fangling's place had long been fixed; Emperor Wen changed it in a single morning, opening the source of rebellion and feeding covetous hopes.

sentences.zh: 又維城肇建，崇其威重，恃寵而驕，厚自封植，進之既逾制，退之不以道。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the wall of the realm was first established, their authority and weight were exalted; relying on favor they grew arrogant, richly cultivating themselves; advancement already exceeded regulations, and withdrawal was not by the proper way.
translations.idiomatic: When the princely domains were established, their authority was exalted; relying on favor they grew arrogant and enriched themselves—advancement exceeded regulations, and withdrawal was not by proper means.

sentences.zh: 俊以憂卒，實此之由。

translations.literal: Jun died of grief—this was truly the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Jun died of grief—this was truly the cause.

sentences.zh: 俄屬天步方艱，讒人已勝，尺布鬥粟，莫肯相容。

translations.literal: Soon the imperial step grew difficult; slanderers had prevailed. A foot of cloth or a peck of grain—none would tolerate the other.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the times grew difficult and slanderers prevailed; like brothers who would not share a foot of cloth or a peck of grain, none would tolerate the other.

sentences.zh: 秀窺岷蜀之阻，諒起晉陽之甲，成茲亂常之釁，蓋亦有以動之也。

translations.literal: Xiu eyed the barriers of Min and Shu; Liang raised arms at Jinyang—forming these breaches of norm and order, there were surely things that moved them to it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu eyed the barriers of Min and Shu; Liang raised arms at Jinyang—forming these breaches of order, there were surely things that provoked them.

sentences.zh: 《棠棣》之詩徒賦，有鼻之封無期，或幽囚於囹圄，或顛殞於鴆毒。

translations.literal: The Ode to the Cherry-apple was recited in vain; the fief with the nose was without term—some were imprisoned in jail, some perished by poison.
translations.idiomatic: The Ode to the Cherry-apple was recited in vain; princely fiefs brought no peace—some were imprisoned, some perished by poison.

sentences.zh: 本根既絕，枝葉畢剪，十有餘年，宗社淪陷。

translations.literal: Once the root and trunk were severed, the branches and leaves were all cut away; within little more than ten years, the ancestral temple and altars fell.
translations.idiomatic: Once the root was severed, the branches were all cut away; within little more than ten years, the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 自古廢嫡立庶，覆族傾宗者多矣，考其亂亡之禍，未若有隋之酷。

translations.literal: Since ancient times, those who deposed the legitimate heir and installed the illegitimate, overturning clans and toppling ancestral lines, have been many—but examining the calamity of disorder and ruin, none has been as cruel as Sui's.
translations.idiomatic: Since ancient times many who deposed legitimate heirs and installed illegitimate ones have overturned clans—but examining the calamity of ruin, none has been as cruel as Sui's.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「殷鑒不遠，在夏後之世。」

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'Yin's mirror is not far—it is in the age of Xia's successor.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: "Yin's mirror is not far—it is in the age after Xia.

sentences.zh: 後之有國有家者，可不深戒哉！

translations.literal: Those who afterward possess states and families—can they not deeply take warning!
translations.idiomatic: Those who afterward possess states and families—can they not deeply take warning!"
